# Phase 11.4: Cross-Platform E2E Testing - Research

**Researched:** 2026-02-28
**Domain:** CI/CD infrastructure, cross-platform desktop testing, FUSE filesystem testing, cryptographic interop validation
**Confidence:** HIGH (mostly based on existing project code and CI patterns)

## Summary

This phase creates a new CI workflow (`e2e-desktop.yml`) that validates the desktop client (Tauri binary) on all three platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux) against a locally-running backend stack. The core challenge is installing Postgres, IPFS (Kubo), Redis, FUSE drivers, and Xvfb natively on each platform's CI runner since Docker service containers are only available on Linux runners.

The existing project already has all the building blocks: a `--dev-key` auth bypass for headless authentication, a `POST /auth/test-login` endpoint, cross-language crypto test vectors in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/crypto/tests.rs`, and per-platform build jobs in `ci.yml`. The main work is (1) adding artifact upload to existing build jobs, (2) creating a new E2E workflow that downloads those artifacts and runs FUSE-level integration tests, and (3) writing shell/Rust test scripts that exercise file operations through the mounted filesystem.

**Primary recommendation:** Build the E2E workflow as a separate `e2e-desktop.yml` triggered by `workflow_run` (after CI completes). Use `ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres@v8` for cross-platform Postgres, install Kubo v0.34.0 from prebuilt binary, and run the Tauri binary with `--dev-key` for headless auth. Tests are shell scripts (bash/PowerShell) that perform file I/O on the FUSE mount point and verify results. Crypto interop tests are `cargo test` with shared fixture files.

## Standard Stack

### Core

| Tool                                | Version       | Purpose                                | Why Standard                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres` | v8            | Cross-platform Postgres install        | Only action that works on Linux/macOS/Windows without Docker                   |
| Kubo (IPFS)                         | v0.34.0       | Local IPFS node                        | Matches existing Docker image version used in `ci.yml` and `e2e.yml`           |
| Redis                               | 7.x           | BullMQ job scheduling (API dependency) | API requires BullMQ which needs Redis                                          |
| FUSE-T                              | latest (brew) | macOS FUSE driver                      | Already used in `cargo-check-macos` and `build-desktop-macos` CI jobs          |
| WinFsp                              | 2.1.25156     | Windows FUSE driver                    | Already installed in `cargo-check-windows` and `build-desktop-windows` CI jobs |
| libfuse3                            | apt package   | Linux FUSE driver                      | Already installed in `cargo-check-linux` and `build-desktop-linux` CI jobs     |
| `GabrielBB/xvfb-action`             | v1            | Virtual framebuffer for Linux          | Standard action for headless GUI testing; wraps `xvfb-run`                     |
| `actions/upload-artifact`           | v4            | Upload desktop binary from build jobs  | Official GitHub artifact action                                                |
| `actions/download-artifact`         | v4            | Download desktop binary in E2E job     | Official GitHub artifact action                                                |

### Supporting

| Tool                 | Version    | Purpose                                       | When to Use                             |
| -------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `dorny/paths-filter` | v3         | Smart trigger for desktop/crypto path changes | PR trigger filtering                    |
| `actions/cache`      | v4         | Cache Cargo registry and target               | Speed up any Rust compilation if needed |
| `pnpm/action-setup`  | v4         | Install pnpm                                  | API and mock-ipns-routing setup         |
| `actions/setup-node` | v4         | Install Node.js 22                            | API and tooling                         |
| mock-ipns-routing    | local tool | Mock delegated IPNS routing for resolve       | E2E IPNS resolve tests                  |

### Alternatives Considered

| Instead of                          | Could Use                                          | Tradeoff                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres` | Manual brew/choco/apt install                      | Much more YAML per platform; action handles it cross-platform                 |
| Shell script tests                  | Playwright-driven Tauri WebDriver                  | WebDriver doesn't test FUSE mount; overkill for file I/O verification         |
| `dawidd6/action-download-artifact`  | Official `actions/download-artifact` with `run-id` | Official v4 now supports cross-workflow; prefer official                      |
| Separate workflow file              | Add to existing `ci.yml`                           | Keep it separate -- the matrix is complex and should not block non-desktop CI |

## Architecture Patterns

### Workflow Architecture

```
ci.yml (existing, modified)
  build-desktop-{windows,macos,linux}
    + upload-artifact step (NEW)

e2e-desktop.yml (NEW)
  trigger: workflow_run (after ci.yml), workflow_dispatch

  jobs:
    e2e-desktop:
      strategy:
        matrix:
          include:
            - os: macos-latest
              artifact: desktop-macos
              fuse-feature: fuse
            - os: windows-latest
              artifact: desktop-windows
              fuse-feature: winfsp
            - os: ubuntu-22.04
              artifact: desktop-linux
              fuse-feature: fuse
      steps:
        1. Download desktop binary artifact
        2. Install Postgres (action-setup-postgres)
        3. Install Kubo (prebuilt binary)
        4. Install Redis
        5. Install FUSE driver (platform-specific)
        6. Setup Node.js + pnpm
        7. Install monorepo deps + build API
        8. Create .env files
        9. Start API + IPFS daemon + mock-ipns-routing
        10. Run migrations
        11. Run desktop E2E tests (with Xvfb on Linux)
        12. Upload test artifacts on failure
```

### Recommended Test Directory Structure

```
tests/
  e2e-desktop/
    fixtures/
      crypto/
        aes-gcm-vectors.json      # Shared AES-GCM test vectors
        aes-ctr-vectors.json      # Shared AES-CTR test vectors
        metadata-vectors.json     # Folder/file metadata encrypt/decrypt vectors
    scripts/
      test-fuse-operations.sh     # macOS/Linux FUSE file I/O tests
      test-fuse-operations.ps1    # Windows FUSE file I/O tests
      test-round-trip.sh          # API creates data, desktop reads via FUSE
      test-round-trip.ps1         # Windows version
      wait-for-mount.sh           # Poll until mount point is available
      wait-for-mount.ps1          # Windows version
    README.md
```

### Test Execution Model

The desktop binary is launched with `--dev-key` which triggers headless auth:

1. Binary starts, creates webview (hidden), detects `--dev-key`
2. Webview JS calls `POST /auth/test-login` -> gets tokens + keypair
3. Calls `handle_test_login_complete` Tauri command
4. `complete_auth_setup` stores keys, inits/fetches vault, registers device, mounts FUSE
5. FUSE mount appears at `~/CipherBox` (macOS/Linux) or `C:\CipherBox` (Windows)
6. Test scripts perform file I/O on mount point
7. Test scripts call API to verify data was encrypted/uploaded correctly
8. Binary is killed, mount is cleaned up

### Pattern: Headless Desktop Launch in CI

```bash
# macOS/Linux
export CIPHERBOX_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
export VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
export VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
export RUST_LOG=info

# Generate a dev key
DEV_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)

# Launch binary in background (debug build for --dev-key support)
./target/debug/cipherbox-desktop --dev-key $DEV_KEY &
DESKTOP_PID=$!

# Wait for FUSE mount to appear
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if mount | grep -q "CipherBox"; then
    echo "Mount detected"
    break
  fi
  sleep 1
done

# Run tests...

# Cleanup
kill $DESKTOP_PID 2>/dev/null
# Force unmount on macOS
diskutil unmount force ~/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true
# Force unmount on Linux
fusermount3 -u ~/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true
```

```powershell
# Windows
$env:CIPHERBOX_API_URL = "http://localhost:3000"
$env:VITE_API_URL = "http://localhost:3000"
$env:VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET = "e2e-test-secret-ci-only"
$env:RUST_LOG = "info"

# Generate a dev key
$DEV_KEY = -join ((1..32) | ForEach-Object { '{0:x2}' -f (Get-Random -Max 256) })

# Launch binary in background
$proc = Start-Process -FilePath ".\target\debug\cipherbox-desktop.exe" `
  -ArgumentList "--dev-key",$DEV_KEY -PassThru -NoNewWindow

# Wait for mount (WinFsp mounts as drive letter or folder)
$timeout = 60
for ($i = 0; $i -lt $timeout; $i++) {
  if (Test-Path "C:\CipherBox") {
    Write-Host "Mount detected"
    break
  }
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 1
}

# Run tests...

# Cleanup
Stop-Process -Id $proc.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

### Pattern: FUSE File I/O Test

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
MOUNT_POINT=~/CipherBox

echo "=== Test: Create and read file ==="
echo "Hello from CI" > "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt"
sleep 2  # Wait for debounced IPNS publish
CONTENT=$(cat "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt")
[ "$CONTENT" = "Hello from CI" ] || { echo "FAIL: content mismatch"; exit 1; }
echo "PASS: file create/read"

echo "=== Test: Create directory ==="
mkdir -p "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder"
[ -d "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder" ] || { echo "FAIL: directory not created"; exit 1; }
echo "PASS: mkdir"

echo "=== Test: Write file in subdirectory ==="
echo "Nested content" > "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder/nested.txt"
sleep 2
NESTED=$(cat "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder/nested.txt")
[ "$NESTED" = "Nested content" ] || { echo "FAIL: nested content mismatch"; exit 1; }
echo "PASS: nested file"

echo "=== Test: Delete file ==="
rm "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt"
sleep 2
[ ! -f "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt" ] || { echo "FAIL: file not deleted"; exit 1; }
echo "PASS: delete"

echo "=== Test: Binary file round-trip ==="
dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/test-binary.bin bs=1024 count=512 2>/dev/null
cp /tmp/test-binary.bin "$MOUNT_POINT/test-binary.bin"
sleep 3  # Larger file needs more time for upload
CHECKSUM_ORIG=$(shasum -a 256 /tmp/test-binary.bin | cut -d' ' -f1)
CHECKSUM_MOUNT=$(shasum -a 256 "$MOUNT_POINT/test-binary.bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)
[ "$CHECKSUM_ORIG" = "$CHECKSUM_MOUNT" ] || { echo "FAIL: binary checksum mismatch"; exit 1; }
echo "PASS: binary round-trip"

echo "All FUSE tests passed!"
```

### Pattern: API Round-Trip Verification

After desktop writes a file via FUSE, verify the API can see the encrypted data:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
API_URL=http://localhost:3000
TEST_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
TEST_EMAIL="e2e-desktop-$(date +%s)@test.local"

# 1. Authenticate via test-login
AUTH_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "$API_URL/auth/test-login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"email\":\"$TEST_EMAIL\",\"secret\":\"$TEST_SECRET\"}")
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(echo "$AUTH_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.accessToken')

# 2. After desktop writes "test-file.txt" via FUSE, check vault API
# The API should show the file in the root folder metadata
VAULT_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  "$API_URL/vault")
ROOT_IPNS=$(echo "$VAULT_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.rootIpnsName')

# 3. Verify IPNS resolve returns valid encrypted metadata
IPNS_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  "$API_URL/ipns/$ROOT_IPNS/resolve")
# Should return a CID pointing to encrypted folder metadata
echo "IPNS resolved: $IPNS_RESPONSE"
```

### Anti-Patterns to Avoid

- **Don't rebuild Rust from source in E2E jobs:** Cargo builds take 10-20 minutes per platform. Download the binary artifact from the build job instead.
- **Don't use Docker service containers on macOS/Windows runners:** Only `ubuntu-*` runners support `services:` blocks. Everything must be natively installed.
- **Don't use release builds for E2E:** The `--dev-key` flag is `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` only. Must use debug builds.
- **Don't assume the mount is instant:** FUSE mount requires auth -> vault fetch -> metadata decrypt -> FUSE init. Budget 30-60 seconds for mount readiness.
- **Don't skip Redis:** The API's `BullModule` (BullMQ) requires Redis. The app will fail to start without it.
- **Don't hardcode mount paths:** macOS/Linux use `~/CipherBox`, Windows may use `C:\CipherBox` or a drive letter. Parameterize.

## Don't Hand-Roll

| Problem                     | Don't Build                 | Use Instead                                                        | Why                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Cross-platform Postgres     | Shell scripts per OS        | `ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres@v8`                             | Handles brew/choco/apt + service startup + createdb + connection URI     |
| Cross-platform IPFS         | Complex conditional install | Kubo prebuilt binary from dist.ipfs.tech                           | Official distribution, no build required, same approach on all platforms |
| Headless GUI on Linux       | Manual Xvfb setup           | `GabrielBB/xvfb-action@v1`                                         | Handles install, startup, cleanup; no-op on non-Linux (safe in matrix)   |
| Cross-platform test runner  | Custom test framework       | Shell scripts (bash + PowerShell)                                  | FUSE tests are file I/O -- shell is the natural tool                     |
| Crypto interop test vectors | Generate at runtime         | Checked-in JSON fixtures from existing `generate-test-vectors.mjs` | Deterministic, version-controlled, already proven                        |

## Common Pitfalls

### Pitfall 1: Docker Services Only Work on Linux Runners

**What goes wrong:** Using `services:` block in a job that runs on `macos-latest` or `windows-latest` fails silently or errors.
**Why it happens:** GitHub Actions only supports Docker service containers on Linux runners.
**How to avoid:** Install all dependencies (Postgres, IPFS, Redis) natively on macOS and Windows using brew/choco/actions.
**Warning signs:** `services:` in a job with `matrix.os` that includes non-Linux.

### Pitfall 2: Existing Build Jobs Don't Upload Artifacts

**What goes wrong:** The E2E job can't download the desktop binary because it was never uploaded.
**Why it happens:** Current `build-desktop-*` jobs in `ci.yml` use `tauri-action` but don't have `upload-artifact` steps.
**How to avoid:** Add `actions/upload-artifact@v4` to each `build-desktop-*` job. The binary is at `apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/cipherbox-desktop` (debug build for `--dev-key` support). Note: `tauri-action` builds a release binary by default, so we either need a separate debug build step or adjust the approach.
**Warning signs:** "Artifact not found" errors in the E2E workflow.

### Pitfall 3: Debug vs Release Build for --dev-key

**What goes wrong:** The `--dev-key` flag and `handle_test_login_complete` command are gated behind `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`. Release builds strip them.
**Why it happens:** Security measure to prevent dev auth bypass in production.
**How to avoid:** The E2E workflow must build or use debug binaries, not the release binaries from `tauri-action`. Options: (a) add a separate `cargo build --debug` step in the build job and upload that artifact, (b) add a Cargo feature flag like `e2e-testing` that enables test-login support in release builds, or (c) build debug in the E2E job itself (slow but simple).
**Warning signs:** "Unknown argument --dev-key" when launching the binary.

### Pitfall 4: Redis Requirement

**What goes wrong:** NestJS API fails to start because BullMQ can't connect to Redis.
**Why it happens:** `app.module.ts` imports `BullModule.forRootAsync()` which requires Redis.
**How to avoid:** Install Redis on each platform: `brew install redis && brew services start redis` (macOS), `choco install redis-64` (Windows), `sudo apt install redis-server && sudo systemctl start redis` (Linux).
**Warning signs:** API startup errors mentioning `ECONNREFUSED :6379`.

### Pitfall 5: FUSE-T Requires Reboot on macOS (WRONG -- it doesn't)

**What goes wrong:** Confusion between FUSE-T and macFUSE/osxfuse.
**Why it happens:** Old macFUSE required kernel extension + reboot. FUSE-T uses userspace NFS/SMB server, no kext, no reboot.
**How to avoid:** Use `brew install --cask fuse-t` (already done in existing CI). This is a non-issue.
**Warning signs:** N/A -- just documenting to prevent future confusion.

### Pitfall 6: Kubo Daemon Startup Race

**What goes wrong:** Tests start before IPFS daemon is fully ready.
**Why it happens:** `ipfs daemon &` backgrounds the process but the API is not immediately available.
**How to avoid:** Poll `curl -s http://localhost:5001/api/v0/id` until it returns HTTP 200 before proceeding.
**Warning signs:** API IPFS operations fail with connection refused.

### Pitfall 7: macOS Finder Interference with FUSE Mount

**What goes wrong:** macOS creates `.DS_Store` files in the mount point, which pollute tests.
**Why it happens:** Finder automatically indexes directories.
**How to avoid:** The desktop app already filters `.DS_Store` in FUSE operations. But test scripts should ignore/filter these files in directory listings. Also, CI runners run headless so Finder interference is minimal.
**Warning signs:** Unexpected `.DS_Store` files in test assertions.

### Pitfall 8: Windows Path Differences

**What goes wrong:** Tests use Unix path separators or `~` which don't work on Windows.
**Why it happens:** Different path conventions across platforms.
**How to avoid:** Use separate shell scripts for Windows (PowerShell `.ps1`) and Unix (bash `.sh`). Don't try to make one script work everywhere.
**Warning signs:** "File not found" errors on Windows.

### Pitfall 9: Cross-Workflow Artifact Download Requires Token Permissions

**What goes wrong:** `actions/download-artifact` can't find artifacts from the CI workflow.
**Why it happens:** v4 requires explicit `run-id` for cross-workflow downloads, or `workflow_run` trigger provides the run context.
**How to avoid:** Use `workflow_run` trigger which provides `github.event.workflow_run.id` for artifact lookups. Or use `dawidd6/action-download-artifact` which searches by workflow name.
**Warning signs:** "Unable to find any artifacts" errors.

## Code Examples

### Cross-Platform Postgres Setup (ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres)

```yaml
# Source: https://github.com/ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres
- name: Setup PostgreSQL
  uses: ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres@v8
  with:
    username: postgres
    password: postgres
    database: cipherbox_test
    postgres-version: '16'
  id: postgres
```

Outputs: `steps.postgres.outputs.connection-uri` for connection string.

### Cross-Platform Kubo Install

```yaml
# Linux/macOS
- name: Install Kubo (IPFS)
  if: runner.os != 'Windows'
  run: |
    KUBO_VERSION="v0.34.0"
    if [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ]; then
      ARCH="darwin-$(uname -m | sed 's/arm64/arm64/' | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/')"
    else
      ARCH="linux-amd64"
    fi
    wget -q "https://dist.ipfs.tech/kubo/${KUBO_VERSION}/kubo_${KUBO_VERSION}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
    tar -xzf "kubo_${KUBO_VERSION}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
    sudo ./kubo/install.sh
    ipfs init
    ipfs daemon &
    # Wait for daemon
    for i in $(seq 1 30); do
      if curl -s http://localhost:5001/api/v0/id > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "IPFS daemon ready"
        break
      fi
      sleep 1
    done

# Windows
- name: Install Kubo (IPFS)
  if: runner.os == 'Windows'
  shell: powershell
  run: |
    $version = "v0.34.0"
    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://dist.ipfs.tech/kubo/$version/kubo_${version}_windows-amd64.zip" -OutFile kubo.zip
    Expand-Archive -Path kubo.zip -DestinationPath .
    $env:PATH = "$PWD\kubo;$env:PATH"
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("PATH", "$PWD\kubo;$env:PATH", "Process")
    ipfs init
    Start-Process -FilePath "ipfs" -ArgumentList "daemon" -NoNewWindow
    # Wait for daemon
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 30; $i++) {
      try {
        $null = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://localhost:5001/api/v0/id" -ErrorAction Stop
        Write-Host "IPFS daemon ready"
        break
      } catch { Start-Sleep -Seconds 1 }
    }
```

### Cross-Platform Redis Install

```yaml
- name: Install Redis
  run: |
    if [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ]; then
      brew install redis
      brew services start redis
    else
      sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y redis-server
      sudo systemctl start redis-server
    fi
  if: runner.os != 'Windows'

- name: Install Redis (Windows)
  if: runner.os == 'Windows'
  shell: powershell
  run: |
    choco install redis-64 -y
    Start-Process redis-server -NoNewWindow
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
```

### WinFsp Install (Already Proven in CI)

```yaml
# Source: .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 362-370
- name: Install WinFsp
  if: runner.os == 'Windows'
  shell: powershell
  run: |
    $url = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.1/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
    $out = "winfsp.msi"
    $expectedHash = "073A70E00F77423E34BED98B86E600DEF93393BA5822204FAC57A29324DB9F7A"
    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out
    $actualHash = (Get-FileHash $out -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) { throw "WinFsp MSI hash mismatch" }
    Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i","$out","/qn","INSTALLLEVEL=1000" -Wait -NoNewWindow
```

### Upload Debug Binary from Build Job

```yaml
# Added to build-desktop-{platform} jobs in ci.yml
- name: Build debug binary for E2E
  run: cargo build --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --no-default-features --features ${{ matrix.fuse-feature }}

- name: Upload debug desktop binary
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: desktop-debug-${{ matrix.os }}
    path: |
      apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/cipherbox-desktop
      apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/cipherbox-desktop.exe
    retention-days: 1
```

### Xvfb for Headless Tauri on Linux

```yaml
# Source: https://github.com/GabrielBB/xvfb-action
- name: Run desktop E2E tests
  uses: GabrielBB/xvfb-action@v1
  if: runner.os == 'Linux'
  with:
    run: ./tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/run-all.sh

- name: Run desktop E2E tests (non-Linux)
  if: runner.os != 'Linux'
  run: ./tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/run-all.sh # or .ps1 for Windows
```

Note: `GabrielBB/xvfb-action` is a no-op on non-Linux, so it could also be used unconditionally, but explicit platform separation is clearer.

### Crypto Interop Test Vector Format (JSON fixtures)

```json
{
  "aes_gcm": {
    "key": "REDACTED",
    "iv": "aabbccddeeff00112233aabb",
    "plaintext_hex": "48656c6c6f2c2043697068657242 6f7821",
    "plaintext_utf8": "Hello, CipherBox!",
    "ciphertext_hex": "196a1416ae4cf2abbd0bb8bdd7dd16be5527207b3c04f9e0a0acf4274fdccbdd5e"
  },
  "aes_ctr": {
    "key": "REDACTED",
    "iv": "aabbccddeeff001122334455aabbccdd",
    "plaintext_hex": "...",
    "ciphertext_hex": "..."
  }
}
```

These fixtures are loaded by both `cargo test` (Rust) and a Node.js validation script, proving cross-platform crypto compatibility.

## State of the Art

| Old Approach                                        | Current Approach                        | When Changed         | Impact                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Docker services for all CI                          | Native installs on macOS/Windows        | Always been required | No Docker on non-Linux runners               |
| `actions/download-artifact` v3 (same workflow only) | v4 supports cross-workflow via `run-id` | 2024                 | Can download from build workflow             |
| macFUSE (kernel extension, requires reboot)         | FUSE-T (userspace, no reboot)           | 2023                 | macOS CI runners can use FUSE without reboot |
| Single CI workflow for everything                   | Separate `e2e-desktop.yml`              | Best practice        | Isolation, different trigger patterns        |

**Deprecated/outdated:**

- macFUSE/osxfuse: Requires kernel extension + reboot. Replaced by FUSE-T for CI.
- `dawidd6/action-download-artifact`: Was needed when official action didn't support cross-workflow. Official v4 now handles this with `run-id`.

## Key Decisions for Planning

### Debug Build Strategy

The biggest architectural decision: how to get a debug binary for E2E testing.

**Option A: Build debug binary in existing build jobs (RECOMMENDED)**

- Add `cargo build` (debug) step to each `build-desktop-*` job in `ci.yml`
- Upload as artifact alongside the release build
- Pros: Leverages existing Cargo cache, runs in parallel with release build
- Cons: Adds ~5-8 min to build jobs (but cached target dir helps)

**Option B: Build debug binary in E2E workflow**

- Full Rust build in the E2E job itself
- Pros: Self-contained workflow
- Cons: No Cargo cache (cold build), adds 15-20 min per platform, duplicates existing build infra

**Option C: Add `e2e-testing` Cargo feature**

- Enable `--dev-key` and `handle_test_login_complete` in release builds when feature is active
- Pros: Can use the release binary from `tauri-action`
- Cons: Requires code changes to `main.rs`, less clean separation

**Recommendation:** Option A. The existing build jobs already have Cargo caches. Adding a debug build step is minimal overhead.

### Workflow Trigger Strategy

**`workflow_run` trigger (RECOMMENDED):**

```yaml
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI']
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
```

- Runs after CI completes on main (or manual dispatch)
- Can access CI workflow's artifacts via `github.event.workflow_run.id`
- Does NOT run on PRs by default (saves CI minutes)

**For PR testing, add path-filtered trigger:**

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'apps/desktop/**'
      - 'packages/crypto/**'
      - 'tests/e2e-desktop/**'
      - '.github/workflows/e2e-desktop.yml'
```

- But this requires building the binary in the PR workflow since CI artifacts may not be ready
- Alternative: Only run on `main` pushes and manual dispatch; PR authors can trigger manually

### Test Output Format

**Standard cargo test output + script exit codes (RECOMMENDED):**

- Crypto interop tests: `cargo test --manifest-path ... -- --test-threads=1`
- FUSE tests: Shell scripts with `set -e` and explicit pass/fail messages
- JUnit XML: Optional, via `cargo-nextest` for Rust or manual XML generation for shell tests

## Open Questions

1. **Windows mount point location:**
   - macOS/Linux mount at `~/CipherBox`
   - Windows: Is it `C:\CipherBox` or a drive letter? Need to check `fuse/windows/mod.rs` mount function
   - Recommendation: Read the code to determine mount path, parameterize in test scripts

2. **macOS runner architecture:**
   - `macos-latest` now runs on Apple Silicon (arm64)
   - The existing `build-desktop-macos` job works on `macos-latest`, so this should be fine
   - But Kubo binary download needs `darwin-arm64` not `darwin-amd64`
   - Recommendation: Auto-detect architecture in install script

3. **Tauri webview on CI:**
   - The binary creates a hidden webview for auth even in `--dev-key` mode
   - On Linux, this requires Xvfb for WebKitGTK
   - On macOS, the runner may have a display; if not, need to set `LSUIElement` or similar
   - On Windows, WebView2 should work headless
   - Recommendation: Use `GabrielBB/xvfb-action` on Linux; test macOS/Windows without Xvfb first

4. **IPNS publish timing in tests:**
   - FUSE write triggers debounced IPNS publish (1.5s debounce, 10s safety valve)
   - Test scripts need adequate `sleep` between write and verification
   - Recommendation: Use generous waits (5-10s) in CI tests; speed is not critical

5. **Concurrent test isolation:**
   - Each platform run uses a unique test email (timestamp-based)
   - But all share the same Postgres DB on the same runner
   - Recommendation: This is fine since each runner has its own stack; no cross-runner sharing

6. **Windows Redis availability:**
   - `choco install redis-64` may not provide the latest version or may be unreliable
   - Alternative: Use `memurai` (Redis-compatible Windows server) or skip BullMQ in test mode
   - Recommendation: Try chocolatey first; if unreliable, use `tporadowski/redis` releases directly

- `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs` -- `handle_test_login_complete`, `complete_auth_setup`

- `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/api/src/auth/auth.controller.ts` -- `POST /auth/test-login` endpoint
- `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/api/src/auth/auth.service.ts` -- `testLogin()` implementation with deterministic keypair
- `/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/api/src/app.module.ts` -- BullMQ Redis dependency confirmed

### Secondary (MEDIUM confidence)

- [ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres](https://github.com/ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres) -- Cross-platform Postgres action, v8, supports PostgreSQL 14-18
- [GabrielBB/xvfb-action](https://github.com/GabrielBB/xvfb-action) -- Xvfb wrapper for GitHub Actions

- [Tauri CI docs](https://v2.tauri.app/develop/tests/webdriver/ci/) -- Xvfb recommendation for Linux

### Tertiary (LOW confidence)

- Redis on Windows via Chocolatey -- community package, reliability unverified
- `actions/download-artifact` v4 cross-workflow support -- documented but specifics of `run-id` passing need validation

## Metadata

**Confidence breakdown:**

- Standard stack: HIGH -- based entirely on existing CI patterns and official GitHub Actions
- Architecture: HIGH -- all components (dev-key auth, test-login, FUSE mount, crypto tests) already exist in the codebase
- Pitfalls: HIGH -- identified from actual CI YAML analysis and code review

### Phase 11.4: Cross-Platform E2E Testing (INSERTED)

**Goal**: Validate that each desktop client (Windows, macOS, Linux) can round-trip correctly against the API and web client — proving cross-platform data integrity, encryption compatibility, and sync correctness without requiring cross-runner coordination
**Depends on**: Phase 11 (Windows Desktop), Phase 11.1 (macOS Desktop Catch-Up), Phase 11.3 (Linux Desktop — all platform clients must exist)
**Requirements**: E2E-01, E2E-02, E2E-03, E2E-04, E2E-05
**Research flag**: NEEDS `/gsd:research-phase` -- Native Postgres/IPFS installation on macOS + Windows CI runners, Tauri command-level testing without full GUI, CI matrix strategy for shared test suite across 3 platforms
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):

1. Each platform CI runner (Windows, macOS, Linux) can start a local backend stack (API + Postgres + IPFS) using native installs (no Docker on macOS/Windows)
2. API/web creates test data (vault, folders, files) and desktop client reads it correctly via Tauri commands or FUSE mount
3. Desktop client creates/modifies data and API/web verifies the changes are correctly encrypted and accessible
4. Cross-platform crypto round-trip tests pass: content encrypted on platform A can be decrypted by platform B's crypto layer
5. IPNS sync round-trip works: metadata published by one client is resolved correctly by another client on the same runner
6. CI test matrix runs all 3 platforms with shared test definitions (no per-platform test duplication)

**Plans**: TBD

### Phase 12: Core Kit Identity Provider Foundation

**Goal**: Replace PnP Modal SDK with MPC Core Kit and establish CipherBox backend as the identity provider for Web3Auth, building the foundation for MFA, SIWE, and cross-device approval in subsequent phases

1→# Phase 11.4: Cross-Platform E2E Testing - Research
     2→
     3→**Researched:** 2026-02-28
     4→**Domain:** CI/CD infrastructure, cross-platform desktop testing, FUSE filesystem testing, cryptographic interop validation
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH (mostly based on existing project code and CI patterns)
     6→
     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→This phase creates a new CI workflow (`e2e-desktop.yml`) that validates the desktop client (Tauri binary) on all three platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux) against a locally-running backend stack. The core challenge is installing Postgres, IPFS (Kubo), Redis, FUSE drivers, and Xvfb natively on each platform's CI runner since Docker service containers are only available on Linux runners.
    10→
    11→The existing project already has all the building blocks: a `--dev-key` auth bypass for headless authentication, a `POST /auth/test-login` endpoint, cross-language crypto test vectors in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/crypto/tests.rs`, and per-platform build jobs in `ci.yml`. The main work is (1) adding artifact upload to existing build jobs, (2) creating a new E2E workflow that downloads those artifacts and runs FUSE-level integration tests, and (3) writing shell/Rust test scripts that exercise file operations through the mounted filesystem.
    12→
    13→**Primary recommendation:** Build the E2E workflow as a separate `e2e-desktop.yml` triggered by `workflow_run` (after CI completes). Use `ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres@v8` for cross-platform Postgres, install Kubo v0.34.0 from prebuilt binary, and run the Tauri binary with `--dev-key` for headless auth. Tests are shell scripts (bash/PowerShell) that perform file I/O on the FUSE mount point and verify results. Crypto interop tests are `cargo test` with shared fixture files.

   111→### Test Execution Model
   112→
   113→The desktop binary is launched with `--dev-key` which triggers headless auth:
   114→
   115→1. Binary starts, creates webview (hidden), detects `--dev-key`
   116→2. Webview JS calls `POST /auth/test-login` -> gets tokens + keypair
   117→3. Calls `handle_test_login_complete` Tauri command
   118→4. `complete_auth_setup` stores keys, inits/fetches vault, registers device, mounts FUSE
   119→5. FUSE mount appears at `~/CipherBox` (macOS/Linux) or `C:\CipherBox` (Windows)
   120→6. Test scripts perform file I/O on mount point
   121→7. Test scripts call API to verify data was encrypted/uploaded correctly
   122→8. Binary is killed, mount is cleaned up
   123→
   124→### Pattern: Headless Desktop Launch in CI
   125→
   126→```bash
   127→# macOS/Linux
   128→export CIPHERBOX_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
   129→export VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
   130→export VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
   131→export RUST_LOG=info
   132→
   133→# Generate a dev key
   134→DEV_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
   135→
   136→# Launch binary in background (debug build for --dev-key support)
   137→./target/debug/cipherbox-desktop --dev-key $DEV_KEY &
   138→DESKTOP_PID=$!
   139→
   140→# Wait for FUSE mount to appear
   141→for i in $(seq 1 60); do
   142→  if mount | grep -q "CipherBox"; then
   143→    echo "Mount detected"
   144→    break
   145→  fi
   146→  sleep 1
   147→done
   148→
   149→# Run tests...
   150→
   151→# Cleanup
   152→kill $DESKTOP_PID 2>/dev/null
   153→# Force unmount on macOS
   154→diskutil unmount force ~/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true
   155→# Force unmount on Linux
   156→fusermount3 -u ~/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true

   189→### Pattern: FUSE File I/O Test
   190→
   191→```bash
   192→#!/bin/bash
   193→set -euo pipefail
   194→MOUNT_POINT=~/CipherBox
   195→
   196→echo "=== Test: Create and read file ==="
   197→echo "Hello from CI" > "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt"
   198→sleep 2  # Wait for debounced IPNS publish
   199→CONTENT=$(cat "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt")
   200→[ "$CONTENT" = "Hello from CI" ] || { echo "FAIL: content mismatch"; exit 1; }
   201→echo "PASS: file create/read"
   202→
   203→echo "=== Test: Create directory ==="
   204→mkdir -p "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder"
   205→[ -d "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder" ] || { echo "FAIL: directory not created"; exit 1; }
   206→echo "PASS: mkdir"
   207→
   208→echo "=== Test: Write file in subdirectory ==="
   209→echo "Nested content" > "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder/nested.txt"
   210→sleep 2
   211→NESTED=$(cat "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder/nested.txt")
   212→[ "$NESTED" = "Nested content" ] || { echo "FAIL: nested content mismatch"; exit 1; }
   213→echo "PASS: nested file"
   214→
   215→echo "=== Test: Delete file ==="
   216→rm "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt"
   217→sleep 2
   218→[ ! -f "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt" ] || { echo "FAIL: file not deleted"; exit 1; }
   219→echo "PASS: delete"
   220→
   221→echo "=== Test: Binary file round-trip ==="
   222→dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/test-binary.bin bs=1024 count=512 2>/dev/null
   223→cp /tmp/test-binary.bin "$MOUNT_POINT/test-binary.bin"
   224→sleep 3  # Larger file needs more time for upload
   225→CHECKSUM_ORIG=$(shasum -a 256 /tmp/test-binary.bin | cut -d' ' -f1)
   226→CHECKSUM_MOUNT=$(shasum -a 256 "$MOUNT_POINT/test-binary.bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)
   227→[ "$CHECKSUM_ORIG" = "$CHECKSUM_MOUNT" ] || { echo "FAIL: binary checksum mismatch"; exit 1; }
   228→echo "PASS: binary round-trip"
   229→
   230→echo "All FUSE tests passed!"
   231→```
   232→
   233→### Pattern: API Round-Trip Verification
   234→
   235→After desktop writes a file via FUSE, verify the API can see the encrypted data:
   236→
   237→```bash
   238→#!/bin/bash
   239→set -euo pipefail
   240→API_URL=http://localhost:3000
   241→TEST_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
   242→TEST_EMAIL="e2e-desktop-$(date +%s)@test.local"
   243→
   244→# 1. Authenticate via test-login
   245→AUTH_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "$API_URL/auth/test-login" \
   246→  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   247→  -d "{\"email\":\"$TEST_EMAIL\",\"secret\":\"$TEST_SECRET\"}")
   248→ACCESS_TOKEN=$(echo "$AUTH_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.accessToken')
   249→
   250→# 2. After desktop writes "test-file.txt" via FUSE, check vault API
   251→# The API should show the file in the root folder metadata
   252→VAULT_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
   253→  "$API_URL/vault")
   254→ROOT_IPNS=$(echo "$VAULT_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.rootIpnsName')
   255→
   256→# 3. Verify IPNS resolve returns valid encrypted metadata
   257→IPNS_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
   258→  "$API_URL/ipns/$ROOT_IPNS/resolve")
   259→# Should return a CID pointing to encrypted folder metadata
   260→echo "IPNS resolved: $IPNS_RESPONSE"
   261→```
   262→
   263→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   264→
   265→- **Don't rebuild Rust from source in E2E jobs:** Cargo builds take 10-20 minutes per platform. Download the binary artifact from the build job instead.
   266→- **Don't use Docker service containers on macOS/Windows runners:** Only `ubuntu-*` runners support `services:` blocks. Everything must be natively installed.
   267→- **Don't use release builds for E2E:** The `--dev-key` flag is `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` only. Must use debug builds.
   268→- **Don't assume the mount is instant:** FUSE mount requires auth -> vault fetch -> metadata decrypt -> FUSE init. Budget 30-60 seconds for mount readiness.
   269→- **Don't skip Redis:** The API's `BullModule` (BullMQ) requires Redis. The app will fail to start without it.
   270→- **Don't hardcode mount paths:** macOS/Linux use `~/CipherBox`, Windows may use `C:\CipherBox` or a drive letter. Parameterize.
   271→
   272→## Don't Hand-Roll
   273→
   274→| Problem                     | Don't Build                 | Use Instead                                                        | Why                                                                      |
   275→| --------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
   276→| Cross-platform Postgres     | Shell scripts per OS        | `ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres@v8`                             | Handles brew/choco/apt + service startup + createdb + connection URI     |
   277→| Cross-platform IPFS         | Complex conditional install | Kubo prebuilt binary from dist.ipfs.tech                           | Official distribution, no build required, same approach on all platforms |
   278→| Headless GUI on Linux       | Manual Xvfb setup           | `GabrielBB/xvfb-action@v1`                                         | Handles install, startup, cleanup; no-op on non-Linux (safe in matrix)   |
   279→| Cross-platform test runner  | Custom test framework       | Shell scripts (bash + PowerShell)                                  | FUSE tests are file I/O -- shell is the natural tool                     |
   280→| Crypto interop test vectors | Generate at runtime         | Checked-in JSON fixtures from existing `generate-test-vectors.mjs` | Deterministic, version-controlled, already proven                        |

   282→## Common Pitfalls
   283→
   284→### Pitfall 1: Docker Services Only Work on Linux Runners
   285→
   286→**What goes wrong:** Using `services:` block in a job that runs on `macos-latest` or `windows-latest` fails silently or errors.
   287→**Why it happens:** GitHub Actions only supports Docker service containers on Linux runners.
   288→**How to avoid:** Install all dependencies (Postgres, IPFS, Redis) natively on macOS and Windows using brew/choco/actions.
   289→**Warning signs:** `services:` in a job with `matrix.os` that includes non-Linux.
   290→
   291→### Pitfall 2: Existing Build Jobs Don't Upload Artifacts
   292→
   293→**What goes wrong:** The E2E job can't download the desktop binary because it was never uploaded.
   294→**Why it happens:** Current `build-desktop-*` jobs in `ci.yml` use `tauri-action` but don't have `upload-artifact` steps.
   295→**How to avoid:** Add `actions/upload-artifact@v4` to each `build-desktop-*` job. The binary is at `apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/cipherbox-desktop` (debug build for `--dev-key` support). Note: `tauri-action` builds a release binary by default, so we either need a separate debug build step or adjust the approach.
   296→**Warning signs:** "Artifact not found" errors in the E2E workflow.
   297→
   298→### Pitfall 3: Debug vs Release Build for --dev-key
   299→
   300→**What goes wrong:** The `--dev-key` flag and `handle_test_login_complete` command are gated behind `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`. Release builds strip them.
   301→**Why it happens:** Security measure to prevent dev auth bypass in production.
   302→**How to avoid:** The E2E workflow must build or use debug binaries, not the release binaries from `tauri-action`. Options: (a) add a separate `cargo build --debug` step in the build job and upload that artifact, (b) add a Cargo feature flag like `e2e-testing` that enables test-login support in release builds, or (c) build debug in the E2E job itself (slow but simple).
   303→**Warning signs:** "Unknown argument --dev-key" when launching the binary.
   304→
   305→### Pitfall 4: Redis Requirement
   306→
   307→**What goes wrong:** NestJS API fails to start because BullMQ can't connect to Redis.
   308→**Why it happens:** `app.module.ts` imports `BullModule.forRootAsync()` which requires Redis.
   309→**How to avoid:** Install Redis on each platform: `brew install redis && brew services start redis` (macOS), `choco install redis-64` (Windows), `sudo apt install redis-server && sudo systemctl start redis` (Linux).
   310→**Warning signs:** API startup errors mentioning `ECONNREFUSED :6379`.
   311→
   312→### Pitfall 5: FUSE-T Requires Reboot on macOS (WRONG -- it doesn't)
   313→
   314→**What goes wrong:** Confusion between FUSE-T and macFUSE/osxfuse.
   315→**Why it happens:** Old macFUSE required kernel extension + reboot. FUSE-T uses userspace NFS/SMB server, no kext, no reboot.
   316→**How to avoid:** Use `brew install --cask fuse-t` (already done in existing CI). This is a non-issue.
   317→**Warning signs:** N/A -- just documenting to prevent future confusion.
   318→
   319→### Pitfall 6: Kubo Daemon Startup Race
   320→
   321→**What goes wrong:** Tests start before IPFS daemon is fully ready.
   322→**Why it happens:** `ipfs daemon &` backgrounds the process but the API is not immediately available.
   323→**How to avoid:** Poll `curl -s http://localhost:5001/api/v0/id` until it returns HTTP 200 before proceeding.
   324→**Warning signs:** API IPFS operations fail with connection refused.
   325→
   326→### Pitfall 7: macOS Finder Interference with FUSE Mount
   327→
   328→**What goes wrong:** macOS creates `.DS_Store` files in the mount point, which pollute tests.
   329→**Why it happens:** Finder automatically indexes directories.
   330→**How to avoid:** The desktop app already filters `.DS_Store` in FUSE operations. But test scripts should ignore/filter these files in directory listings. Also, CI runners run headless so Finder interference is minimal.
   331→**Warning signs:** Unexpected `.DS_Store` files in test assertions.
   332→
   333→### Pitfall 8: Windows Path Differences
   334→
   335→**What goes wrong:** Tests use Unix path separators or `~` which don't work on Windows.
   336→**Why it happens:** Different path conventions across platforms.
   337→**How to avoid:** Use separate shell scripts for Windows (PowerShell `.ps1`) and Unix (bash `.sh`). Don't try to make one script work everywhere.
   338→**Warning signs:** "File not found" errors on Windows.
   339→
   340→### Pitfall 9: Cross-Workflow Artifact Download Requires Token Permissions
   341→
   342→**What goes wrong:** `actions/download-artifact` can't find artifacts from the CI workflow.
   343→**Why it happens:** v4 requires explicit `run-id` for cross-workflow downloads, or `workflow_run` trigger provides the run context.
   344→**How to avoid:** Use `workflow_run` trigger which provides `github.event.workflow_run.id` for artifact lookups. Or use `dawidd6/action-download-artifact` which searches by workflow name.
   345→**Warning signs:** "Unable to find any artifacts" errors.

   365→### Cross-Platform Kubo Install
   366→
   367→```yaml
   368→# Linux/macOS
   369→- name: Install Kubo (IPFS)
   370→  if: runner.os != 'Windows'
   371→  run: |
   372→    KUBO_VERSION="v0.34.0"
   373→    if [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ]; then
   374→      ARCH="darwin-$(uname -m | sed 's/arm64/arm64/' | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/')"
   375→    else
   376→      ARCH="linux-amd64"
   377→    fi
   378→    wget -q "https://dist.ipfs.tech/kubo/${KUBO_VERSION}/kubo_${KUBO_VERSION}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
   379→    tar -xzf "kubo_${KUBO_VERSION}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
   380→    sudo ./kubo/install.sh
   381→    ipfs init
   382→    ipfs daemon &
   383→    # Wait for daemon
   384→    for i in $(seq 1 30); do
   385→      if curl -s http://localhost:5001/api/v0/id > /dev/null 2>&1; then
   386→        echo "IPFS daemon ready"
   387→        break
   388→      fi
   389→      sleep 1
   390→    done
   391→
   392→# Windows
   393→- name: Install Kubo (IPFS)
   394→  if: runner.os == 'Windows'
   395→  shell: powershell
   396→  run: |
   397→    $version = "v0.34.0"
   398→    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://dist.ipfs.tech/kubo/$version/kubo_${version}_windows-amd64.zip" -OutFile kubo.zip
   399→    Expand-Archive -Path kubo.zip -DestinationPath .
   400→    $env:PATH = "$PWD\kubo;$env:PATH"
   401→    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("PATH", "$PWD\kubo;$env:PATH", "Process")
   402→    ipfs init
   403→    Start-Process -FilePath "ipfs" -ArgumentList "daemon" -NoNewWindow
   404→    # Wait for daemon
   405→    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 30; $i++) {
   406→      try {
   407→        $null = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://localhost:5001/api/v0/id" -ErrorAction Stop
   408→        Write-Host "IPFS daemon ready"
   409→        break
   410→      } catch { Start-Sleep -Seconds 1 }
   411→    }
   412→```

   510→## State of the Art
   511→
   512→| Old Approach                                        | Current Approach                        | When Changed         | Impact                                       |
   513→| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
   514→| Docker services for all CI                          | Native installs on macOS/Windows        | Always been required | No Docker on non-Linux runners               |
   515→| `actions/download-artifact` v3 (same workflow only) | v4 supports cross-workflow via `run-id` | 2024                 | Can download from build workflow             |
   516→| macFUSE (kernel extension, requires reboot)         | FUSE-T (userspace, no reboot)           | 2023                 | macOS CI runners can use FUSE without reboot |
   517→| Single CI workflow for everything                   | Separate `e2e-desktop.yml`              | Best practice        | Isolation, different trigger patterns        |
   518→
   519→**Deprecated/outdated:**
   520→
   521→- macFUSE/osxfuse: Requires kernel extension + reboot. Replaced by FUSE-T for CI.
   522→- `dawidd6/action-download-artifact`: Was needed when official action didn't support cross-workflow. Official v4 now handles this with `run-id`.

   524→## Key Decisions for Planning
   525→
   526→### Debug Build Strategy
   527→
   528→The biggest architectural decision: how to get a debug binary for E2E testing.
   529→
   530→**Option A: Build debug binary in existing build jobs (RECOMMENDED)**
   531→
   532→- Add `cargo build` (debug) step to each `build-desktop-*` job in `ci.yml`
   533→- Upload as artifact alongside the release build
   534→- Pros: Leverages existing Cargo cache, runs in parallel with release build
   535→- Cons: Adds ~5-8 min to build jobs (but cached target dir helps)
   536→
   537→**Option B: Build debug binary in E2E workflow**
   538→
   539→- Full Rust build in the E2E job itself
   540→- Pros: Self-contained workflow
   541→- Cons: No Cargo cache (cold build), adds 15-20 min per platform, duplicates existing build infra
   542→
   543→**Option C: Add `e2e-testing` Cargo feature**
   544→
   545→- Enable `--dev-key` and `handle_test_login_complete` in release builds when feature is active
   546→- Pros: Can use the release binary from `tauri-action`
   547→- Cons: Requires code changes to `main.rs`, less clean separation
   548→
   549→**Recommendation:** Option A. The existing build jobs already have Cargo caches. Adding a debug build step is minimal overhead.
   550→
   551→### Workflow Trigger Strategy
   552→
   553→**`workflow_run` trigger (RECOMMENDED):**
   554→
   555→```yaml
   556→on:
   557→  workflow_run:
   558→    workflows: ['CI']
   559→    types: [completed]
   560→    branches: [main]
   561→  workflow_dispatch:
   562→```
   563→
   564→- Runs after CI completes on main (or manual dispatch)
   565→- Can access CI workflow's artifacts via `github.event.workflow_run.id`
   566→- Does NOT run on PRs by default (saves CI minutes)
   567→
   568→**For PR testing, add path-filtered trigger:**
   569→
   570→```yaml
   571→on:
   572→  pull_request:
   573→    branches: [main]
   574→    paths:
   575→      - 'apps/desktop/**'
   576→      - 'packages/crypto/**'
   577→      - 'tests/e2e-desktop/**'
   578→      - '.github/workflows/e2e-desktop.yml'
   579→```
   580→
   581→- But this requires building the binary in the PR workflow since CI artifacts may not be ready
   582→- Alternative: Only run on `main` pushes and manual dispatch; PR authors can trigger manually
   583→
   584→### Test Output Format
   585→
   586→**Standard cargo test output + script exit codes (RECOMMENDED):**
   587→
   588→- Crypto interop tests: `cargo test --manifest-path ... -- --test-threads=1`
   589→- FUSE tests: Shell scripts with `set -e` and explicit pass/fail messages
   590→- JUnit XML: Optional, via `cargo-nextest` for Rust or manual XML generation for shell tests

   592→## Open Questions
   593→
   594→1. **Windows mount point location:**
   595→   - macOS/Linux mount at `~/CipherBox`
   596→   - Windows: Is it `C:\CipherBox` or a drive letter? Need to check `fuse/windows/mod.rs` mount function
   597→   - Recommendation: Read the code to determine mount path, parameterize in test scripts
   598→
   599→2. **macOS runner architecture:**
   600→   - `macos-latest` now runs on Apple Silicon (arm64)
   601→   - The existing `build-desktop-macos` job works on `macos-latest`, so this should be fine
   602→   - But Kubo binary download needs `darwin-arm64` not `darwin-amd64`
   603→   - Recommendation: Auto-detect architecture in install script
   604→
   605→3. **Tauri webview on CI:**
   606→   - The binary creates a hidden webview for auth even in `--dev-key` mode
   607→   - On Linux, this requires Xvfb for WebKitGTK
   608→   - On macOS, the runner may have a display; if not, need to set `LSUIElement` or similar
   609→   - On Windows, WebView2 should work headless
   610→   - Recommendation: Use `GabrielBB/xvfb-action` on Linux; test macOS/Windows without Xvfb first
   611→
   612→4. **IPNS publish timing in tests:**
   613→   - FUSE write triggers debounced IPNS publish (1.5s debounce, 10s safety valve)
   614→   - Test scripts need adequate `sleep` between write and verification
   615→   - Recommendation: Use generous waits (5-10s) in CI tests; speed is not critical
   616→
   617→5. **Concurrent test isolation:**
   618→   - Each platform run uses a unique test email (timestamp-based)
   619→   - But all share the same Postgres DB on the same runner
   620→   - Recommendation: This is fine since each runner has its own stack; no cross-runner sharing
   621→
   622→6. **Windows Redis availability:**
   623→   - `choco install redis-64` may not provide the latest version or may be unreliable
   624→   - Alternative: Use `memurai` (Redis-compatible Windows server) or skip BullMQ in test mode
   625→   - Recommendation: Try chocolatey first; if unreliable, use `tporadowski/redis` releases directly

   400→### Phase 15: Link Sharing
   401→
   402→**Goal**: Users can share files and folders via invite links where the decryption key lives in the URL fragment only (never sent to server). Recipients must authenticate (invite model) and the share is auto-claimed using Phase 14 infrastructure.
   403→**Depends on**: Phase 14
   404→**Requirements**: SHARE-06, SHARE-07
   405→**Research flag**: COMPLETE -- ephemeral key bridge pattern, HashRouter fragment handling, unauthenticated endpoint design researched
   406→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   407→
   408→1. User can generate a shareable link for a file where the decryption key is in the URL fragment only (never sent to server)
   409→2. Recipient can open the link, log in or create an account, and the share is auto-claimed (appears in "Shared with me")
   410→
   411→**Plans:** 4 plans

   413→Plans:
   414→
   415→- [x] 15-01-PLAN.md — Backend: ShareInvite entity, migration, DTOs, InvitesController, service methods, module registration

   417→- [x] 15-03-PLAN.md — ShareDialog tabbed UI (Direct Share | Invite Link) + InvitePage landing page + route + build verification
   418→- [x] 15-04-PLAN.md — E2E test suite: Playwright page objects + invite-link-workflow.spec.ts

   420→### Phase 15.1: Client-Side Search (INSERTED)
   421→
   422→**Goal**: Users can search file and folder names across their entire vault with an encrypted search index persisted in IndexedDB
   423→**Depends on**: Phase 15
   424→**Requirements**: SRCH-01, SRCH-02, SRCH-03
   425→**Research flag**: Standard patterns -- minisearch + idb (per research), skip `/gsd:research-phase`
   426→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   427→
   428→1. User can search file names across all folders and see matching results with navigation to the file location
   429→2. Search index is encrypted and persisted in IndexedDB, surviving page refreshes
   430→3. Search index updates incrementally when IPNS polling detects metadata changes
   431→
   432→**Plans:** 3 plans

   434→Plans:
   435→
   436→- [x] 15.1-01-PLAN.md — Search index service: minisearch setup, HKDF-derived AES-GCM encrypted IndexedDB persistence, folder tree indexing

   438→- [x] 15.1-03-PLAN.md — E2E test suite: SearchPalettePage page object + search-workflow.spec.ts (gap closure)

   440→### Phase 16: Advanced Sync
   441→
   442→**Goal**: Users experience reliable sync with conflict awareness and offline resilience
   443→**Depends on**: Phase 15
   444→**Requirements**: SYNC-04, SYNC-05, SYNC-06
   445→**Research flag**: NEEDS `/gsd:research-phase` -- three-way merge edge cases with encrypted metadata need exhaustive test matrix. Offline replay with idempotency keys is uncharted territory for this codebase.
   446→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   447→
   448→1. Client detects when another device has published a newer IPNS sequence number and alerts the user before overwriting
   449→2. When the user goes offline and makes changes, operations are queued locally and automatically replayed on reconnect
   450→3. Queued operations use idempotency keys so replaying them after reconnect never produces duplicate files or folders
   451→   **Plans**: TBD
   452→
   453→### Phase 17: AWS Nitro TEE
   454→
   455→**Goal**: IPNS republishing has a fallback TEE provider for high availability
   456→**Depends on**: Phase 12 (can run in parallel with Phases 14-16 after MFA stabilizes auth)
   457→**Requirements**: TEE-06
   458→**Research flag**: NEEDS `/gsd:research-phase` -- Rust enclave binary, vsock communication, KMS attestation are entirely new technology for this project. Highest-risk item in M2.
   459→**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
   460→
   461→1. AWS Nitro enclave can receive ECIES-encrypted IPNS keys, decrypt in hardware, sign IPNS records, and zero memory
   462→2. Backend routes republish jobs to Nitro when Phala Cloud is unavailable, with automatic failover and failback

   210→      - name: Check for entity/migration drift
   211→        working-directory: apps/api
   212→        run: |
   213→          set +e
   214→          OUTPUT="$(pnpm typeorm migration:generate src/migrations/DriftCheck -d src/data-source.ts 2>&1)"
   215→          STATUS=$?
   216→          set -e
   217→
   218→          # Check if migration:generate failed before inspecting output files
   219→          if [ "$STATUS" -ne 0 ]; then
   220→            if echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q "No changes in database schema were found"; then
   221→              echo "No entity/migration drift detected."
   222→              exit 0
   223→            fi
   224→            echo "::error::migration:generate failed unexpectedly."
   225→            echo "$OUTPUT"
   226→            exit 1
   227→          fi
   228→
   229→          if ls src/migrations/*DriftCheck*.ts 1>/dev/null 2>&1; then
   230→            # Our hand-written migrations use explicit constraint/index names, but TypeORM
   231→            # expects auto-generated hash-based names. Filter out cosmetic renames and only
   232→            # fail on real structural drift (new/dropped tables, added/removed columns, type changes).
   233→            if grep -qE 'CREATE TABLE|DROP TABLE|ADD COLUMN|DROP COLUMN|ALTER.*TYPE|RENAME COLUMN' src/migrations/*DriftCheck*.ts; then
   234→              echo "::error::Entity/migration drift detected! Entities define schema changes not covered by migrations."
   235→              echo ""
   236→              echo "Generated migration contents:"
   237→              cat src/migrations/*DriftCheck*.ts
   238→              echo ""
   239→              echo "Fix: Run 'pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api typeorm migration:generate src/migrations/<Name> -d src/data-source.ts' and commit the result."
   240→              exit 1
   241→            else
   242→              echo "Only cosmetic constraint/index naming differences detected (not structural drift). OK."
   243→            fi
   244→          else
   245→            echo "No entity/migration drift detected."
   246→          fi

1→# Desktop Client Testing Strategy
     2→
     3→**Date:** 2026-02-08
     4→
     5→## Original Prompt
     6→
     7→> Phase 9 UAT revealed that every test required manual human interaction because Web3Auth login cannot be automated. This makes CI/CD and agent-driven testing impossible.
     8→
     9→## What I Learned
    10→
    11→### The Web3Auth Testing Wall
    12→
    13→- Web3Auth login requires a real browser interaction (Google OAuth, email OTP, etc.). There is no headless/programmatic bypass in the SDK.
    14→- Every UAT test required a human to: click Login in tray, complete Web3Auth flow, wait for FUSE mount, then test the actual feature.
    15→- This made iterative debugging painfully slow — each fix required a full rebuild + manual login cycle.
    16→- Agent-assisted development (Claude) could diagnose issues from logs and write fixes, but could never verify them independently.
    17→
    18→### Proposed Solution: Auth Bypass for Development
    19→
    20→A `--dev-key <hex-private-key>` CLI argument that bypasses Web3Auth entirely:
    21→
    22→1. Accept a secp256k1 private key via CLI arg or environment variable (`CIPHERBOX_DEV_KEY`)
    23→2. Derive the public key from it
    24→3. Call the API's `/auth/login` endpoint directly (the API already accepts `{ publicKey, loginType: "desktop" }`)
    25→4. Store the resulting JWT and proceed to FUSE mount
    26→
    27→This enables:
    28→
    29→- **Automated testing:** Playwright/script can launch app with `--dev-key`, test FUSE operations, quit
    30→- **Agent-driven UAT:** Claude can launch the app, verify FUSE behavior via `ls`/`cat`/`echo`, and iterate without human intervention
    31→- **CI integration:** Spin up API + app with test key, run filesystem operation tests
    32→- **Faster debugging:** Skip the 15-second Web3Auth flow on every iteration
    33→
    34→### Implementation Notes
    35→
    36→- Gate behind `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` or a `dev` feature flag — never ship in release builds
    37→- The test account's private key can live in `tests/e2e/.env` alongside existing test credentials
    38→- Key derivation: `secp256k1::SecretKey::from_slice(&hex::decode(key))` -> compressed public key -> `/auth/login`
    39→- After auth, the flow joins the normal path: fetch vault metadata, mount FUSE, start sync
    40→
    41→### What Else Would Help
    42→
    43→- **FUSE unit tests:** Test the `CipherBoxFS` struct directly without mounting. Mock the API client, call `lookup()`, `readdir()`, `read()` etc. as method calls. This tests all the NFS-sensitive logic (inode stability, cache behavior, platform file filtering) without needing a real mount.
    44→- **Integration test script:** A shell script that exercises FUSE operations after mount: `ls`, `cat`, `echo >`, `mkdir`, `mv`, `rm`, and verifies results. Combined with `--dev-key`, this gives end-to-end coverage.
    45→- **Snapshot testing for inode table:** Serialize the inode table state after `populate_folder()`, compare against known-good snapshots. Catches inode stability regressions.
    46→
    47→### Testing Priorities for Linux/Windows Ports
    48→
    49→1. **Start with the auth bypass** — get FUSE mounting testable without UI interaction
    50→2. **Port the FUSE unit tests first** — the inode table and cache logic is shared
    51→3. **Platform-specific tests:** Linux FUSE has different behavior (multithreaded, no NFS translation). Windows WinFSP has its own quirks. Each needs platform-specific test coverage.
    52→4. **The channel-based prefetch pattern** should have its own test — verify that content arrives via channel and cache is populated correctly
    53→
    54→## Key Files
    55→
    56→- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` — CLI argument parsing (add `--dev-key` here)
    57→- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs` — `handle_auth_complete` (the flow to join after bypass auth)
    58→- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/api/auth.rs` — API auth calls
    59→- `tests/e2e/.env` — Test credentials
    60→

### Phase 12.6: Per-File IPNS Metadata Split (INSERTED)

**Goal**: Split file metadata into separate per-file IPNS-addressed objects so content updates don't require folder republishes, and per-file sharing becomes possible
**Depends on**: Phase 12.5 (MFA polish complete, clean-break window before vault wipe)
**Requirements**: Foundation for SHARE-01 (per-file sharing), VER-01 (version history in file metadata), performance improvement for content updates

**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):

2. Folder metadata contains only file name fields + fileMetaIpnsName pointer — no embedded CIDs or file keys
3. Content update (re-upload) publishes only the file's IPNS record, not the parent folder's
4. File rename publishes only the folder IPNS record, not the file's
5. Batch operations (multi-file upload) publish all file IPNS records in a single API call (preserving Phase 7.1 atomicity)
6. TEE republisher handles per-file IPNS records with acceptable scalability (defined during research)
7. Desktop FUSE client reads per-file IPNS metadata correctly
8. Vault export includes per-file metadata in portable format

**Requirements**: SHARE-01, SHARE-02, SHARE-03, SHARE-04, SHARE-05

**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):

3. User can revoke a share, which triggers lazy folderKey rotation on the next folder modification
4. Recipient can browse shared folders in a "Shared with me" section at ~/shared
5. Server never sees plaintext folderKey or fileKey at any point during the sharing flow

2. Recipient can open the link, log in or create an account, and the share is auto-claimed (appears in "Shared with me")

**Plans:** 4 plans

Plans:

- [x] 15-01-PLAN.md — Backend: ShareInvite entity, migration, DTOs, InvitesController, service methods, module registration
- [x] 15-02-PLAN.md — API client regen + frontend invite service with ephemeral key bridge crypto
- [x] 15-03-PLAN.md — ShareDialog tabbed UI (Direct Share | Invite Link) + InvitePage landing page + route + build verification
- [x] 15-04-PLAN.md — E2E test suite: Playwright page objects + invite-link-workflow.spec.ts

### Phase 15.1: Client-Side Search (INSERTED)

**Goal**: Users can search file and folder names across their entire vault with an encrypted search index persisted in IndexedDB
**Depends on**: Phase 15
**Requirements**: SRCH-01, SRCH-02, SRCH-03
**Research flag**: Standard patterns -- minisearch + idb (per research), skip `/gsd:research-phase`
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):

1. User can search file names across all folders and see matching results with navigation to the file location
2. Search index is encrypted and persisted in IndexedDB, surviving page refreshes
3. Search index updates incrementally when IPNS polling detects metadata changes

**Plans:** 3 plans

Plans:

- [x] 15.1-01-PLAN.md — Search index service: minisearch setup, HKDF-derived AES-GCM encrypted IndexedDB persistence, folder tree indexing
- [x] 15.1-02-PLAN.md — Search UI (command palette overlay), useSearch hook, sync integration, AppHeader/AppShell wiring, human verification
- [x] 15.1-03-PLAN.md — E2E test suite: SearchPalettePage page object + search-workflow.spec.ts (gap closure)

### Phase 16: Advanced Sync

**Goal**: Users experience reliable sync with conflict awareness and offline resilience
**Depends on**: Phase 15
**Requirements**: SYNC-04, SYNC-05, SYNC-06
**Research flag**: NEEDS `/gsd:research-phase` -- three-way merge edge cases with encrypted metadata need exhaustive test matrix. Offline replay with idempotency keys is uncharted territory for this codebase.
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):

1. Client detects when another device has published a newer IPNS sequence number and alerts the user before overwriting
2. When the user goes offline and makes changes, operations are queued locally and automatically replayed on reconnect
3. Queued operations use idempotency keys so replaying them after reconnect never produces duplicate files or folders
   **Plans**: TBD

### Phase 17: AWS Nitro TEE

**Goal**: IPNS republishing has a fallback TEE provider for high availability
**Depends on**: Phase 12 (can run in parallel with Phases 14-16 after MFA stabilizes auth)
**Requirements**: TEE-06
**Research flag**: NEEDS `/gsd:research-phase` -- Rust enclave binary, vsock communication, KMS attestation are entirely new technology for this project. Highest-risk item in M2.
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):

1. AWS Nitro enclave can receive ECIES-encrypted IPNS keys, decrypt in hardware, sign IPNS records, and zero memory
2. Backend routes republish jobs to Nitro when Phala Cloud is unavailable, with automatic failover and failback
   **Plans**: TBD

Sequential order: 12 -> 12.5 -> 12.6 -> 12.1 -> 11.2 -> 13 -> 14 -> 15 -> 15.1 -> 16 -> 17 -> 18 -> 19 -> 20 -> 21

    99→**Job: e2e-desktop**
   100→
   101→```yaml
   102→jobs:
   103→  e2e-desktop:
   104→    name: Desktop E2E (${{ matrix.platform }})
   105→    if: >-
   106→      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
   107→      (github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success')
   108→    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
   109→    timeout-minutes: 30
   110→    strategy:
   111→      fail-fast: false
   112→      matrix:
   113→        include:
   114→          - platform: macos
   115→            os: macos-latest
   116→            artifact: desktop-debug-macos
   117→            fuse-feature: fuse
   118→            shell: bash
   119→          - platform: windows
   120→            os: windows-latest
   121→            artifact: desktop-debug-windows
   122→            fuse-feature: winfsp
   123→            shell: powershell
   124→          - platform: linux
   125→            os: ubuntu-22.04
   126→            artifact: desktop-debug-linux
   127→            fuse-feature: fuse
   128→            shell: bash

   131→**Steps (in order):**
   132→
   133→1. **Checkout** -- `actions/checkout@v4`
   134→
   135→2. **Download debug binary** -- Use `actions/download-artifact@v4` with:
   136→   - `name: ${{ matrix.artifact }}`
   137→   - `path: desktop-binary/`
   138→   - `run-id: ${{ inputs.run_id || github.event.workflow_run.id }}`
   139→   - `github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`
   140→     If `workflow_dispatch` without `run_id`, we need the latest CI run. Use a step that finds it:
   141→
   142→   ```yaml
   143→   - name: Find latest CI run ID
   144→     if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.run_id == ''
   145→     id: find-run
   146→     run: |
   147→       RUN_ID=$(gh run list --workflow=ci.yml --branch=main --status=success --limit=1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')
   148→       echo "run_id=$RUN_ID" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
   149→     env:
   150→       GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
   151→   ```
   152→
   153→   Then the download step uses: `run-id: ${{ inputs.run_id || steps.find-run.outputs.run_id || github.event.workflow_run.id }}`

    14→## Implementation Decisions
    15→
    16→### CI backend stack
    17→

    19→- Fresh NestJS API backend per CI run with empty database — full isolation, no staging pollution
    20→- Cache the cargo-built desktop binary from existing build jobs and download it in the E2E job (avoid rebuilding Rust from scratch)
    21→
    22→### CI trigger strategy
    23→
    24→- Smart trigger: run on PRs only when desktop or crypto paths change (path filter)

    26→- Manual workflow_dispatch available for ad-hoc runs
    27→

    29→

    32→- Launch the actual Tauri app binary in test mode (--test flag or env var), not standalone Rust test binary
    33→- Authenticate via dev-key auth (POST /auth/test-login) — no Web3Auth/Core Kit in CI

1→# Phase 11.4: Cross-Platform E2E Testing - Research
     2→
     3→**Researched:** 2026-02-28
     4→**Domain:** CI/CD infrastructure, cross-platform desktop testing, FUSE filesystem testing, cryptographic interop validation
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH (mostly based on existing project code and CI patterns)
     6→
     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→This phase creates a new CI workflow (`e2e-desktop.yml`) that validates the desktop client (Tauri binary) on all three platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux) against a locally-running backend stack. The core challenge is installing Postgres, IPFS (Kubo), Redis, FUSE drivers, and Xvfb natively on each platform's CI runner since Docker service containers are only available on Linux runners.
    10→
    11→The existing project already has all the building blocks: a `--dev-key` auth bypass for headless authentication, a `POST /auth/test-login` endpoint, cross-language crypto test vectors in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/crypto/tests.rs`, and per-platform build jobs in `ci.yml`. The main work is (1) adding artifact upload to existing build jobs, (2) creating a new E2E workflow that downloads those artifacts and runs FUSE-level integration tests, and (3) writing shell/Rust test scripts that exercise file operations through the mounted filesystem.
    12→
    13→**Primary recommendation:** Build the E2E workflow as a separate `e2e-desktop.yml` triggered by `workflow_run` (after CI completes). Use `ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres@v8` for cross-platform Postgres, install Kubo v0.34.0 from prebuilt binary, and run the Tauri binary with `--dev-key` for headless auth. Tests are shell scripts (bash/PowerShell) that perform file I/O on the FUSE mount point and verify results. Crypto interop tests are `cargo test` with shared fixture files.

   110→
   111→### Test Execution Model
   112→
   113→The desktop binary is launched with `--dev-key` which triggers headless auth:
   114→
   115→1. Binary starts, creates webview (hidden), detects `--dev-key`
   116→2. Webview JS calls `POST /auth/test-login` -> gets tokens + keypair
   117→3. Calls `handle_test_login_complete` Tauri command
   118→4. `complete_auth_setup` stores keys, inits/fetches vault, registers device, mounts FUSE
   119→5. FUSE mount appears at `~/CipherBox` (macOS/Linux) or `C:\CipherBox` (Windows)
   120→6. Test scripts perform file I/O on mount point
   121→7. Test scripts call API to verify data was encrypted/uploaded correctly
   122→8. Binary is killed, mount is cleaned up
   123→
   124→### Pattern: Headless Desktop Launch in CI
   125→
   126→```bash
   127→# macOS/Linux
   128→export CIPHERBOX_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
   129→export VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
   130→export VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
   131→export RUST_LOG=info
   132→
   133→# Generate a dev key
   134→DEV_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
   135→
   136→# Launch binary in background (debug build for --dev-key support)
   137→./target/debug/cipherbox-desktop --dev-key $DEV_KEY &
   138→DESKTOP_PID=$!
   139→
   140→# Wait for FUSE mount to appear
   141→for i in $(seq 1 60); do
   142→  if mount | grep -q "CipherBox"; then
   143→    echo "Mount detected"
   144→    break
   145→  fi
   146→  sleep 1
   147→done
   148→
   149→# Run tests...
   150→
   151→# Cleanup
   152→kill $DESKTOP_PID 2>/dev/null
   153→# Force unmount on macOS
   154→diskutil unmount force ~/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true
   155→# Force unmount on Linux
   156→fusermount3 -u ~/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true
   157→```
   158→
   159→```powershell
   160→# Windows
   161→$env:CIPHERBOX_API_URL = "http://localhost:3000"
   162→$env:VITE_API_URL = "http://localhost:3000"
   163→$env:VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET = "e2e-test-secret-ci-only"
   164→$env:RUST_LOG = "info"
   165→
   166→# Generate a dev key
   167→$DEV_KEY = -join ((1..32) | ForEach-Object { '{0:x2}' -f (Get-Random -Max 256) })
   168→
   169→# Launch binary in background
   170→$proc = Start-Process -FilePath ".\target\debug\cipherbox-desktop.exe" `
   171→  -ArgumentList "--dev-key",$DEV_KEY -PassThru -NoNewWindow
   172→
   173→# Wait for mount (WinFsp mounts as drive letter or folder)

   175→for ($i = 0; $i -lt $timeout; $i++) {
   176→  if (Test-Path "C:\CipherBox") {
   177→    Write-Host "Mount detected"
   178→    break
   179→  }
   180→  Start-Sleep -Seconds 1

   182→
   183→# Run tests...
