   188→
   189→### Pattern: FUSE File I/O Test
   190→
   191→```bash
   192→#!/bin/bash
   193→set -euo pipefail
   194→MOUNT_POINT=~/CipherBox
   195→
   196→echo "=== Test: Create and read file ==="
   197→echo "Hello from CI" > "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt"
   198→sleep 2  # Wait for debounced IPNS publish
   199→CONTENT=$(cat "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt")
   200→[ "$CONTENT" = "Hello from CI" ] || { echo "FAIL: content mismatch"; exit 1; }
   201→echo "PASS: file create/read"
   202→
   203→echo "=== Test: Create directory ==="
   204→mkdir -p "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder"
   205→[ -d "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder" ] || { echo "FAIL: directory not created"; exit 1; }
   206→echo "PASS: mkdir"
   207→
   208→echo "=== Test: Write file in subdirectory ==="
   209→echo "Nested content" > "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder/nested.txt"
   210→sleep 2
   211→NESTED=$(cat "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder/nested.txt")
   212→[ "$NESTED" = "Nested content" ] || { echo "FAIL: nested content mismatch"; exit 1; }
   213→echo "PASS: nested file"
   214→
   215→echo "=== Test: Delete file ==="
   216→rm "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt"
   217→sleep 2
   218→[ ! -f "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt" ] || { echo "FAIL: file not deleted"; exit 1; }
   219→echo "PASS: delete"
   220→
   221→echo "=== Test: Binary file round-trip ==="
   222→dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/test-binary.bin bs=1024 count=512 2>/dev/null
   223→cp /tmp/test-binary.bin "$MOUNT_POINT/test-binary.bin"
   224→sleep 3  # Larger file needs more time for upload
   225→CHECKSUM_ORIG=$(shasum -a 256 /tmp/test-binary.bin | cut -d' ' -f1)
   226→CHECKSUM_MOUNT=$(shasum -a 256 "$MOUNT_POINT/test-binary.bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)
   227→[ "$CHECKSUM_ORIG" = "$CHECKSUM_MOUNT" ] || { echo "FAIL: binary checksum mismatch"; exit 1; }
   228→echo "PASS: binary round-trip"
   229→
   230→echo "All FUSE tests passed!"
   231→```
   232→
   233→### Pattern: API Round-Trip Verification
   234→
   235→After desktop writes a file via FUSE, verify the API can see the encrypted data:
   236→
   237→```bash
   238→#!/bin/bash
   239→set -euo pipefail
   240→API_URL=http://localhost:3000
   241→TEST_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
   242→TEST_EMAIL="e2e-desktop-$(date +%s)@test.local"
   243→
   244→# 1. Authenticate via test-login
   245→AUTH_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "$API_URL/auth/test-login" \
   246→  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   247→  -d "{\"email\":\"$TEST_EMAIL\",\"secret\":\"$TEST_SECRET\"}")
   248→ACCESS_TOKEN=$(echo "$AUTH_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.accessToken')
   249→
   250→# 2. After desktop writes "test-file.txt" via FUSE, check vault API
   251→# The API should show the file in the root folder metadata
   252→VAULT_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
   253→  "$API_URL/vault")
   254→ROOT_IPNS=$(echo "$VAULT_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.rootIpnsName')
   255→
   256→# 3. Verify IPNS resolve returns valid encrypted metadata
   257→IPNS_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
   258→  "$API_URL/ipns/$ROOT_IPNS/resolve")
   259→# Should return a CID pointing to encrypted folder metadata
   260→echo "IPNS resolved: $IPNS_RESPONSE"
   261→```
   262→
   263→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   264→
   265→- **Don't rebuild Rust from source in E2E jobs:** Cargo builds take 10-20 minutes per platform. Download the binary artifact from the build job instead.
   266→- **Don't use Docker service containers on macOS/Windows runners:** Only `ubuntu-*` runners support `services:` blocks. Everything must be natively installed.
   267→- **Don't use release builds for E2E:** The `--dev-key` flag is `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` only. Must use debug builds.
   268→- **Don't assume the mount is instant:** FUSE mount requires auth -> vault fetch -> metadata decrypt -> FUSE init. Budget 30-60 seconds for mount readiness.
   269→- **Don't skip Redis:** The API's `BullModule` (BullMQ) requires Redis. The app will fail to start without it.
   270→- **Don't hardcode mount paths:** macOS/Linux use `~/CipherBox`, Windows may use `C:\CipherBox` or a drive letter. Parameterize.
   271→
   272→## Don't Hand-Roll
   273→
   274→| Problem                     | Don't Build                 | Use Instead                                                        | Why                                                                      |
   275→| --------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
   276→| Cross-platform Postgres     | Shell scripts per OS        | `ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres@v8`                             | Handles brew/choco/apt + service startup + createdb + connection URI     |
   277→| Cross-platform IPFS         | Complex conditional install | Kubo prebuilt binary from dist.ipfs.tech                           | Official distribution, no build required, same approach on all platforms |
   278→| Headless GUI on Linux       | Manual Xvfb setup           | `GabrielBB/xvfb-action@v1`                                         | Handles install, startup, cleanup; no-op on non-Linux (safe in matrix)   |
   279→| Cross-platform test runner  | Custom test framework       | Shell scripts (bash + PowerShell)                                  | FUSE tests are file I/O -- shell is the natural tool                     |
   280→| Crypto interop test vectors | Generate at runtime         | Checked-in JSON fixtures from existing `generate-test-vectors.mjs` | Deterministic, version-controlled, already proven                        |
   281→
   282→## Common Pitfalls
   283→
   284→### Pitfall 1: Docker Services Only Work on Linux Runners
   285→
   286→**What goes wrong:** Using `services:` block in a job that runs on `macos-latest` or `windows-latest` fails silently or errors.
   287→**Why it happens:** GitHub Actions only supports Docker service containers on Linux runners.
   288→**How to avoid:** Install all dependencies (Postgres, IPFS, Redis) natively on macOS and Windows using brew/choco/actions.
   289→**Warning signs:** `services:` in a job with `matrix.os` that includes non-Linux.
   290→
   291→### Pitfall 2: Existing Build Jobs Don't Upload Artifacts
   292→
   293→**What goes wrong:** The E2E job can't download the desktop binary because it was never uploaded.
   294→**Why it happens:** Current `build-desktop-*` jobs in `ci.yml` use `tauri-action` but don't have `upload-artifact` steps.
   295→**How to avoid:** Add `actions/upload-artifact@v4` to each `build-desktop-*` job. The binary is at `apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/cipherbox-desktop` (debug build for `--dev-key` support). Note: `tauri-action` builds a release binary by default, so we either need a separate debug build step or adjust the approach.
   296→**Warning signs:** "Artifact not found" errors in the E2E workflow.
   297→
   298→### Pitfall 3: Debug vs Release Build for --dev-key
   299→
   300→**What goes wrong:** The `--dev-key` flag and `handle_test_login_complete` command are gated behind `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`. Release builds strip them.
   301→**Why it happens:** Security measure to prevent dev auth bypass in production.
   302→**How to avoid:** The E2E workflow must build or use debug binaries, not the release binaries from `tauri-action`. Options: (a) add a separate `cargo build --debug` step in the build job and upload that artifact, (b) add a Cargo feature flag like `e2e-testing` that enables test-login support in release builds, or (c) build debug in the E2E job itself (slow but simple).
   303→**Warning signs:** "Unknown argument --dev-key" when launching the binary.
   304→
   305→### Pitfall 4: Redis Requirement
   306→
   307→**What goes wrong:** NestJS API fails to start because BullMQ can't connect to Redis.
   308→**Why it happens:** `app.module.ts` imports `BullModule.forRootAsync()` which requires Redis.
   309→**How to avoid:** Install Redis on each platform: `brew install redis && brew services start redis` (macOS), `choco install redis-64` (Windows), `sudo apt install redis-server && sudo systemctl start redis` (Linux).
   310→**Warning signs:** API startup errors mentioning `ECONNREFUSED :6379`.
   311→
   312→### Pitfall 5: FUSE-T Requires Reboot on macOS (WRONG -- it doesn't)
   313→
   314→**What goes wrong:** Confusion between FUSE-T and macFUSE/osxfuse.
   315→**Why it happens:** Old macFUSE required kernel extension + reboot. FUSE-T uses userspace NFS/SMB server, no kext, no reboot.
   316→**How to avoid:** Use `brew install --cask fuse-t` (already done in existing CI). This is a non-issue.
   317→**Warning signs:** N/A -- just documenting to prevent future confusion.
   318→
   319→### Pitfall 6: Kubo Daemon Startup Race
   320→
   321→**What goes wrong:** Tests start before IPFS daemon is fully ready.
   322→**Why it happens:** `ipfs daemon &` backgrounds the process but the API is not immediately available.
   323→**How to avoid:** Poll `curl -s http://localhost:5001/api/v0/id` until it returns HTTP 200 before proceeding.
   324→**Warning signs:** API IPFS operations fail with connection refused.
   325→
   326→### Pitfall 7: macOS Finder Interference with FUSE Mount
   327→
   328→**What goes wrong:** macOS creates `.DS_Store` files in the mount point, which pollute tests.
   329→**Why it happens:** Finder automatically indexes directories.
   330→**How to avoid:** The desktop app already filters `.DS_Store` in FUSE operations. But test scripts should ignore/filter these files in directory listings. Also, CI runners run headless so Finder interference is minimal.
   331→**Warning signs:** Unexpected `.DS_Store` files in test assertions.
   332→
   333→### Pitfall 8: Windows Path Differences
   334→
   335→**What goes wrong:** Tests use Unix path separators or `~` which don't work on Windows.
   336→**Why it happens:** Different path conventions across platforms.
   337→**How to avoid:** Use separate shell scripts for Windows (PowerShell `.ps1`) and Unix (bash `.sh`). Don't try to make one script work everywhere.
   338→**Warning signs:** "File not found" errors on Windows.
   339→
   340→### Pitfall 9: Cross-Workflow Artifact Download Requires Token Permissions
   341→
   342→**What goes wrong:** `actions/download-artifact` can't find artifacts from the CI workflow.
   343→**Why it happens:** v4 requires explicit `run-id` for cross-workflow downloads, or `workflow_run` trigger provides the run context.
   344→**How to avoid:** Use `workflow_run` trigger which provides `github.event.workflow_run.id` for artifact lookups. Or use `dawidd6/action-download-artifact` which searches by workflow name.
   345→**Warning signs:** "Unable to find any artifacts" errors.

   509→
   510→## State of the Art
   511→
   512→| Old Approach                                        | Current Approach                        | When Changed         | Impact                                       |
   513→| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
   514→| Docker services for all CI                          | Native installs on macOS/Windows        | Always been required | No Docker on non-Linux runners               |
   515→| `actions/download-artifact` v3 (same workflow only) | v4 supports cross-workflow via `run-id` | 2024                 | Can download from build workflow             |
   516→| macFUSE (kernel extension, requires reboot)         | FUSE-T (userspace, no reboot)           | 2023                 | macOS CI runners can use FUSE without reboot |
   517→| Single CI workflow for everything                   | Separate `e2e-desktop.yml`              | Best practice        | Isolation, different trigger patterns        |
   518→
   519→**Deprecated/outdated:**
   520→
   521→- macFUSE/osxfuse: Requires kernel extension + reboot. Replaced by FUSE-T for CI.
   522→- `dawidd6/action-download-artifact`: Was needed when official action didn't support cross-workflow. Official v4 now handles this with `run-id`.
   523→
   524→## Key Decisions for Planning
   525→
   526→### Debug Build Strategy
   527→
   528→The biggest architectural decision: how to get a debug binary for E2E testing.
   529→
   530→**Option A: Build debug binary in existing build jobs (RECOMMENDED)**
   531→
   532→- Add `cargo build` (debug) step to each `build-desktop-*` job in `ci.yml`
   533→- Upload as artifact alongside the release build
   534→- Pros: Leverages existing Cargo cache, runs in parallel with release build
   535→- Cons: Adds ~5-8 min to build jobs (but cached target dir helps)
   536→
   537→**Option B: Build debug binary in E2E workflow**
   538→
   539→- Full Rust build in the E2E job itself
   540→- Pros: Self-contained workflow
   541→- Cons: No Cargo cache (cold build), adds 15-20 min per platform, duplicates existing build infra
   542→
   543→**Option C: Add `e2e-testing` Cargo feature**
   544→
   545→- Enable `--dev-key` and `handle_test_login_complete` in release builds when feature is active
   546→- Pros: Can use the release binary from `tauri-action`
   547→- Cons: Requires code changes to `main.rs`, less clean separation
   548→
   549→**Recommendation:** Option A. The existing build jobs already have Cargo caches. Adding a debug build step is minimal overhead.
   550→
   551→### Workflow Trigger Strategy
   552→
   553→**`workflow_run` trigger (RECOMMENDED):**
   554→
   555→```yaml
   556→on:
   557→  workflow_run:
   558→    workflows: ['CI']
   559→    types: [completed]
   560→    branches: [main]
   561→  workflow_dispatch:
   562→```
   563→
   564→- Runs after CI completes on main (or manual dispatch)
   565→- Can access CI workflow's artifacts via `github.event.workflow_run.id`
   566→- Does NOT run on PRs by default (saves CI minutes)
   567→
   568→**For PR testing, add path-filtered trigger:**
   569→
   570→```yaml
   571→on:
   572→  pull_request:
   573→    branches: [main]
   574→    paths:
   575→      - 'apps/desktop/**'
   576→      - 'packages/crypto/**'
   577→      - 'tests/e2e-desktop/**'
   578→      - '.github/workflows/e2e-desktop.yml'
   579→```
   580→
   581→- But this requires building the binary in the PR workflow since CI artifacts may not be ready
   582→- Alternative: Only run on `main` pushes and manual dispatch; PR authors can trigger manually
   583→
   584→### Test Output Format
   585→
   586→**Standard cargo test output + script exit codes (RECOMMENDED):**
   587→
   588→- Crypto interop tests: `cargo test --manifest-path ... -- --test-threads=1`
   589→- FUSE tests: Shell scripts with `set -e` and explicit pass/fail messages
   590→- JUnit XML: Optional, via `cargo-nextest` for Rust or manual XML generation for shell tests
   591→
   592→## Open Questions
   593→
   594→1. **Windows mount point location:**
   595→   - macOS/Linux mount at `~/CipherBox`
   596→   - Windows: Is it `C:\CipherBox` or a drive letter? Need to check `fuse/windows/mod.rs` mount function
   597→   - Recommendation: Read the code to determine mount path, parameterize in test scripts
   598→
   599→2. **macOS runner architecture:**
   600→   - `macos-latest` now runs on Apple Silicon (arm64)
   601→   - The existing `build-desktop-macos` job works on `macos-latest`, so this should be fine
   602→   - But Kubo binary download needs `darwin-arm64` not `darwin-amd64`
   603→   - Recommendation: Auto-detect architecture in install script
   604→
   605→3. **Tauri webview on CI:**
   606→   - The binary creates a hidden webview for auth even in `--dev-key` mode
   607→   - On Linux, this requires Xvfb for WebKitGTK
   608→   - On macOS, the runner may have a display; if not, need to set `LSUIElement` or similar
   609→   - On Windows, WebView2 should work headless
   610→   - Recommendation: Use `GabrielBB/xvfb-action` on Linux; test macOS/Windows without Xvfb first
   611→
   612→4. **IPNS publish timing in tests:**
   613→   - FUSE write triggers debounced IPNS publish (1.5s debounce, 10s safety valve)
   614→   - Test scripts need adequate `sleep` between write and verification
   615→   - Recommendation: Use generous waits (5-10s) in CI tests; speed is not critical
   616→
   617→5. **Concurrent test isolation:**
   618→   - Each platform run uses a unique test email (timestamp-based)
   619→   - But all share the same Postgres DB on the same runner
   620→   - Recommendation: This is fine since each runner has its own stack; no cross-runner sharing
   621→
   622→6. **Windows Redis availability:**
   623→   - `choco install redis-64` may not provide the latest version or may be unreliable
   624→   - Alternative: Use `memurai` (Redis-compatible Windows server) or skip BullMQ in test mode
   625→   - Recommendation: Try chocolatey first; if unreliable, use `tporadowski/redis` releases directly

   153→
   154→Test cases (each prints PASS/FAIL with descriptive message):
   155→
   156→1. **Create and read text file:** `echo "Hello from CI" > "$MP/e2e-test.txt"`, sleep 3, verify `cat "$MP/e2e-test.txt"` equals "Hello from CI"
   157→2. **Create directory:** `mkdir -p "$MP/e2e-folder"`, verify `test -d "$MP/e2e-folder"`
   158→3. **Write file in subdirectory:** `echo "Nested content" > "$MP/e2e-folder/nested.txt"`, sleep 3, verify content
   159→4. **Overwrite file (modify):** `echo "Modified content" > "$MP/e2e-test.txt"`, sleep 3, verify content changed
   160→5. **Binary file round-trip:** `dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/e2e-binary.bin bs=1024 count=256 2>/dev/null`, `cp /tmp/e2e-binary.bin "$MP/e2e-binary.bin"`, sleep 5 (larger file), verify SHA-256 checksums match. Use `shasum -a 256` on macOS or `sha256sum` on Linux -- detect which is available.
   161→6. **Rename file:** `mv "$MP/e2e-test.txt" "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt"`, sleep 2, verify old doesn't exist and new has correct content
   162→7. **Delete file:** `rm "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt"`, sleep 2, verify file is gone
   163→8. **Delete directory:** `rm -rf "$MP/e2e-folder"`, sleep 2, verify directory is gone
   164→9. **Cleanup:** Remove `$MP/e2e-binary.bin` if it exists, remove `/tmp/e2e-binary.bin`
   165→
   166→Track pass/fail count. Exit with count of failures.
   167→
   168→IMPORTANT: Sleep values must be generous for CI (debounced IPNS publish = 1.5s debounce + upload time). Use 3s for small text files, 5s for binary files. The desktop app's FUSE write -> release() -> encrypt + upload -> publish cycle needs time.

1→# Phase 11.4: Cross-Platform E2E Testing - Research
     2→
     3→**Researched:** 2026-02-28
     4→**Domain:** CI/CD infrastructure, cross-platform desktop testing, FUSE filesystem testing, cryptographic interop validation
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH (mostly based on existing project code and CI patterns)
     6→
     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→This phase creates a new CI workflow (`e2e-desktop.yml`) that validates the desktop client (Tauri binary) on all three platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux) against a locally-running backend stack. The core challenge is installing Postgres, IPFS (Kubo), Redis, FUSE drivers, and Xvfb natively on each platform's CI runner since Docker service containers are only available on Linux runners.
    10→
    11→The existing project already has all the building blocks: a `--dev-key` auth bypass for headless authentication, a `POST /auth/test-login` endpoint, cross-language crypto test vectors in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/crypto/tests.rs`, and per-platform build jobs in `ci.yml`. The main work is (1) adding artifact upload to existing build jobs, (2) creating a new E2E workflow that downloads those artifacts and runs FUSE-level integration tests, and (3) writing shell/Rust test scripts that exercise file operations through the mounted filesystem.
    12→
    13→**Primary recommendation:** Build the E2E workflow as a separate `e2e-desktop.yml` triggered by `workflow_run` (after CI completes). Use `ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres@v8` for cross-platform Postgres, install Kubo v0.34.0 from prebuilt binary, and run the Tauri binary with `--dev-key` for headless auth. Tests are shell scripts (bash/PowerShell) that perform file I/O on the FUSE mount point and verify results. Crypto interop tests are `cargo test` with shared fixture files.
    14→

    50→## Architecture Patterns

   110→
   111→### Test Execution Model
   112→
   113→The desktop binary is launched with `--dev-key` which triggers headless auth:
   114→
   115→1. Binary starts, creates webview (hidden), detects `--dev-key`
   116→2. Webview JS calls `POST /auth/test-login` -> gets tokens + keypair
   117→3. Calls `handle_test_login_complete` Tauri command
   118→4. `complete_auth_setup` stores keys, inits/fetches vault, registers device, mounts FUSE
   119→5. FUSE mount appears at `~/CipherBox` (macOS/Linux) or `C:\CipherBox` (Windows)
   120→6. Test scripts perform file I/O on mount point
   121→7. Test scripts call API to verify data was encrypted/uploaded correctly
   122→8. Binary is killed, mount is cleaned up
   123→
   124→### Pattern: Headless Desktop Launch in CI
   125→
   126→```bash
   127→# macOS/Linux
   128→export CIPHERBOX_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
   129→export VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
   130→export VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
   131→export RUST_LOG=info
   132→
   133→# Generate a dev key
   134→DEV_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
   135→
   136→# Launch binary in background (debug build for --dev-key support)
   137→./target/debug/cipherbox-desktop --dev-key $DEV_KEY &
   138→DESKTOP_PID=$!
   139→
   140→# Wait for FUSE mount to appear
   141→for i in $(seq 1 60); do
   142→  if mount | grep -q "CipherBox"; then
   143→    echo "Mount detected"
   144→    break
   145→  fi
   146→  sleep 1
   147→done
   148→
   149→# Run tests...
   150→
   151→# Cleanup
   152→kill $DESKTOP_PID 2>/dev/null
   153→# Force unmount on macOS
   154→diskutil unmount force ~/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true
   155→# Force unmount on Linux
   156→fusermount3 -u ~/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true

   189→### Pattern: FUSE File I/O Test
   190→
   191→```bash
   192→#!/bin/bash
   193→set -euo pipefail
   194→MOUNT_POINT=~/CipherBox
   195→
   196→echo "=== Test: Create and read file ==="
   197→echo "Hello from CI" > "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt"
   198→sleep 2  # Wait for debounced IPNS publish
   199→CONTENT=$(cat "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt")
   200→[ "$CONTENT" = "Hello from CI" ] || { echo "FAIL: content mismatch"; exit 1; }
   201→echo "PASS: file create/read"
   202→
   203→echo "=== Test: Create directory ==="
   204→mkdir -p "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder"
   205→[ -d "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder" ] || { echo "FAIL: directory not created"; exit 1; }
   206→echo "PASS: mkdir"
   207→
   208→echo "=== Test: Write file in subdirectory ==="
   209→echo "Nested content" > "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder/nested.txt"
   210→sleep 2
   211→NESTED=$(cat "$MOUNT_POINT/test-folder/nested.txt")
   212→[ "$NESTED" = "Nested content" ] || { echo "FAIL: nested content mismatch"; exit 1; }
   213→echo "PASS: nested file"
   214→
   215→echo "=== Test: Delete file ==="
   216→rm "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt"
   217→sleep 2
   218→[ ! -f "$MOUNT_POINT/test-file.txt" ] || { echo "FAIL: file not deleted"; exit 1; }
   219→echo "PASS: delete"
   220→
   221→echo "=== Test: Binary file round-trip ==="
   222→dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/test-binary.bin bs=1024 count=512 2>/dev/null
   223→cp /tmp/test-binary.bin "$MOUNT_POINT/test-binary.bin"
   224→sleep 3  # Larger file needs more time for upload
   225→CHECKSUM_ORIG=$(shasum -a 256 /tmp/test-binary.bin | cut -d' ' -f1)
   226→CHECKSUM_MOUNT=$(shasum -a 256 "$MOUNT_POINT/test-binary.bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)
   227→[ "$CHECKSUM_ORIG" = "$CHECKSUM_MOUNT" ] || { echo "FAIL: binary checksum mismatch"; exit 1; }
   228→echo "PASS: binary round-trip"
   229→
   230→echo "All FUSE tests passed!"
   231→```
   232→
   233→### Pattern: API Round-Trip Verification
   234→
   235→After desktop writes a file via FUSE, verify the API can see the encrypted data:
   236→
   237→```bash
   238→#!/bin/bash
   239→set -euo pipefail
   240→API_URL=http://localhost:3000
   241→TEST_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
   242→TEST_EMAIL="e2e-desktop-$(date +%s)@test.local"
   243→
   244→# 1. Authenticate via test-login
   245→AUTH_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "$API_URL/auth/test-login" \
   246→  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   247→  -d "{\"email\":\"$TEST_EMAIL\",\"secret\":\"$TEST_SECRET\"}")
   248→ACCESS_TOKEN=$(echo "$AUTH_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.accessToken')
   249→
   250→# 2. After desktop writes "test-file.txt" via FUSE, check vault API
   251→# The API should show the file in the root folder metadata
   252→VAULT_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
   253→  "$API_URL/vault")
   254→ROOT_IPNS=$(echo "$VAULT_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.rootIpnsName')
   255→
   256→# 3. Verify IPNS resolve returns valid encrypted metadata
   257→IPNS_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
   258→  "$API_URL/ipns/$ROOT_IPNS/resolve")
   259→# Should return a CID pointing to encrypted folder metadata
   260→echo "IPNS resolved: $IPNS_RESPONSE"
   261→```
   262→
   263→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   264→
   265→- **Don't rebuild Rust from source in E2E jobs:** Cargo builds take 10-20 minutes per platform. Download the binary artifact from the build job instead.
   266→- **Don't use Docker service containers on macOS/Windows runners:** Only `ubuntu-*` runners support `services:` blocks. Everything must be natively installed.
   267→- **Don't use release builds for E2E:** The `--dev-key` flag is `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` only. Must use debug builds.
   268→- **Don't assume the mount is instant:** FUSE mount requires auth -> vault fetch -> metadata decrypt -> FUSE init. Budget 30-60 seconds for mount readiness.
   269→- **Don't skip Redis:** The API's `BullModule` (BullMQ) requires Redis. The app will fail to start without it.
   270→- **Don't hardcode mount paths:** macOS/Linux use `~/CipherBox`, Windows may use `C:\CipherBox` or a drive letter. Parameterize.
   271→
   272→## Don't Hand-Roll
   273→
   274→| Problem                     | Don't Build                 | Use Instead                                                        | Why                                                                      |
   275→| --------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
   276→| Cross-platform Postgres     | Shell scripts per OS        | `ikalnytskyi/action-setup-postgres@v8`                             | Handles brew/choco/apt + service startup + createdb + connection URI     |
   277→| Cross-platform IPFS         | Complex conditional install | Kubo prebuilt binary from dist.ipfs.tech                           | Official distribution, no build required, same approach on all platforms |
   278→| Headless GUI on Linux       | Manual Xvfb setup           | `GabrielBB/xvfb-action@v1`                                         | Handles install, startup, cleanup; no-op on non-Linux (safe in matrix)   |
   279→| Cross-platform test runner  | Custom test framework       | Shell scripts (bash + PowerShell)                                  | FUSE tests are file I/O -- shell is the natural tool                     |
   280→| Crypto interop test vectors | Generate at runtime         | Checked-in JSON fixtures from existing `generate-test-vectors.mjs` | Deterministic, version-controlled, already proven                        |
   281→
   282→## Common Pitfalls
   283→
   284→### Pitfall 1: Docker Services Only Work on Linux Runners
   285→
   286→**What goes wrong:** Using `services:` block in a job that runs on `macos-latest` or `windows-latest` fails silently or errors.
   287→**Why it happens:** GitHub Actions only supports Docker service containers on Linux runners.
   288→**How to avoid:** Install all dependencies (Postgres, IPFS, Redis) natively on macOS and Windows using brew/choco/actions.
   289→**Warning signs:** `services:` in a job with `matrix.os` that includes non-Linux.
   290→
   291→### Pitfall 2: Existing Build Jobs Don't Upload Artifacts
   292→
   293→**What goes wrong:** The E2E job can't download the desktop binary because it was never uploaded.
   294→**Why it happens:** Current `build-desktop-*` jobs in `ci.yml` use `tauri-action` but don't have `upload-artifact` steps.
   295→**How to avoid:** Add `actions/upload-artifact@v4` to each `build-desktop-*` job. The binary is at `apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/cipherbox-desktop` (debug build for `--dev-key` support). Note: `tauri-action` builds a release binary by default, so we either need a separate debug build step or adjust the approach.

   298→### Pitfall 3: Debug vs Release Build for --dev-key
   299→
   300→**What goes wrong:** The `--dev-key` flag and `handle_test_login_complete` command are gated behind `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`. Release builds strip them.
   301→**Why it happens:** Security measure to prevent dev auth bypass in production.
   302→**How to avoid:** The E2E workflow must build or use debug binaries, not the release binaries from `tauri-action`. Options: (a) add a separate `cargo build --debug` step in the build job and upload that artifact, (b) add a Cargo feature flag like `e2e-testing` that enables test-login support in release builds, or (c) build debug in the E2E job itself (slow but simple).

   305→### Pitfall 4: Redis Requirement
   306→
   307→**What goes wrong:** NestJS API fails to start because BullMQ can't connect to Redis.
   308→**Why it happens:** `app.module.ts` imports `BullModule.forRootAsync()` which requires Redis.
   309→**How to avoid:** Install Redis on each platform: `brew install redis && brew services start redis` (macOS), `choco install redis-64` (Windows), `sudo apt install redis-server && sudo systemctl start redis` (Linux).

   312→### Pitfall 5: FUSE-T Requires Reboot on macOS (WRONG -- it doesn't)
   313→
   314→**What goes wrong:** Confusion between FUSE-T and macFUSE/osxfuse.
   315→**Why it happens:** Old macFUSE required kernel extension + reboot. FUSE-T uses userspace NFS/SMB server, no kext, no reboot.
   316→**How to avoid:** Use `brew install --cask fuse-t` (already done in existing CI). This is a non-issue.
   317→**Warning signs:** N/A -- just documenting to prevent future confusion.
   318→
   319→### Pitfall 6: Kubo Daemon Startup Race
   320→
   321→**What goes wrong:** Tests start before IPFS daemon is fully ready.
   322→**Why it happens:** `ipfs daemon &` backgrounds the process but the API is not immediately available.
   323→**How to avoid:** Poll `curl -s http://localhost:5001/api/v0/id` until it returns HTTP 200 before proceeding.
   324→**Warning signs:** API IPFS operations fail with connection refused.
   325→
   326→### Pitfall 7: macOS Finder Interference with FUSE Mount
   327→
   328→**What goes wrong:** macOS creates `.DS_Store` files in the mount point, which pollute tests.
   329→**Why it happens:** Finder automatically indexes directories.
   330→**How to avoid:** The desktop app already filters `.DS_Store` in FUSE operations. But test scripts should ignore/filter these files in directory listings. Also, CI runners run headless so Finder interference is minimal.
   331→**Warning signs:** Unexpected `.DS_Store` files in test assertions.
   332→
   333→### Pitfall 8: Windows Path Differences
   334→
   335→**What goes wrong:** Tests use Unix path separators or `~` which don't work on Windows.
   336→**Why it happens:** Different path conventions across platforms.
   337→**How to avoid:** Use separate shell scripts for Windows (PowerShell `.ps1`) and Unix (bash `.sh`). Don't try to make one script work everywhere.
   338→**Warning signs:** "File not found" errors on Windows.
   339→
   340→### Pitfall 9: Cross-Workflow Artifact Download Requires Token Permissions
   341→
   342→**What goes wrong:** `actions/download-artifact` can't find artifacts from the CI workflow.
   343→**Why it happens:** v4 requires explicit `run-id` for cross-workflow downloads, or `workflow_run` trigger provides the run context.
   344→**How to avoid:** Use `workflow_run` trigger which provides `github.event.workflow_run.id` for artifact lookups. Or use `dawidd6/action-download-artifact` which searches by workflow name.

   510→## State of the Art
   511→
   512→| Old Approach                                        | Current Approach                        | When Changed         | Impact                                       |

   517→| Single CI workflow for everything                   | Separate `e2e-desktop.yml`              | Best practice        | Isolation, different trigger patterns        |

   519→**Deprecated/outdated:**

   522→- `dawidd6/action-download-artifact`: Was needed when official action didn't support cross-workflow. Official v4 now handles this with `run-id`.

   525→
   526→### Debug Build Strategy
   527→
   528→The biggest architectural decision: how to get a debug binary for E2E testing.
   529→
   530→**Option A: Build debug binary in existing build jobs (RECOMMENDED)**
   531→
   532→- Add `cargo build` (debug) step to each `build-desktop-*` job in `ci.yml`
   533→- Upload as artifact alongside the release build
   534→- Pros: Leverages existing Cargo cache, runs in parallel with release build
   535→- Cons: Adds ~5-8 min to build jobs (but cached target dir helps)
   536→
   537→**Option B: Build debug binary in E2E workflow**
   538→
   539→- Full Rust build in the E2E job itself
   540→- Pros: Self-contained workflow
   541→- Cons: No Cargo cache (cold build), adds 15-20 min per platform, duplicates existing build infra
   542→
   543→**Option C: Add `e2e-testing` Cargo feature**
   544→
   545→- Enable `--dev-key` and `handle_test_login_complete` in release builds when feature is active
   546→- Pros: Can use the release binary from `tauri-action`
   547→- Cons: Requires code changes to `main.rs`, less clean separation
   548→
   549→**Recommendation:** Option A. The existing build jobs already have Cargo caches. Adding a debug build step is minimal overhead.
   550→
   551→### Workflow Trigger Strategy
   552→
   553→**`workflow_run` trigger (RECOMMENDED):**
   554→
   555→```yaml
   556→on:
   557→  workflow_run:
   558→    workflows: ['CI']
   559→    types: [completed]
   560→    branches: [main]
   561→  workflow_dispatch:

   573→    branches: [main]

   575→      - 'apps/desktop/**'
   576→      - 'packages/crypto/**'
   577→      - 'tests/e2e-desktop/**'
   578→      - '.github/workflows/e2e-desktop.yml'
   579→```
   580→
   581→- But this requires building the binary in the PR workflow since CI artifacts may not be ready
   582→- Alternative: Only run on `main` pushes and manual dispatch; PR authors can trigger manually
   583→

   585→
   586→**Standard cargo test output + script exit codes (RECOMMENDED):**
   587→
   588→- Crypto interop tests: `cargo test --manifest-path ... -- --test-threads=1`
   589→- FUSE tests: Shell scripts with `set -e` and explicit pass/fail messages

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# wait-for-mount.sh -- Poll until the CipherBox FUSE mount point is available.
#
# Usage: ./wait-for-mount.sh [mount-point]
#   mount-point  Path to check (default: $HOME/CipherBox)
#
# Environment:
#   MOUNT_TIMEOUT  Seconds to wait before failing (default: 90)

MOUNT_POINT="${1:-$HOME/CipherBox}"
TIMEOUT="${MOUNT_TIMEOUT:-90}"
INTERVAL=2
ELAPSED=0

echo "Waiting for mount at $MOUNT_POINT (timeout: ${TIMEOUT}s)..."

while [ "$ELAPSED" -lt "$TIMEOUT" ]; do
  # Check that the mount point directory exists AND that something is mounted there.
  # macOS (FUSE-T SMB backend) shows "smbfs" in mount output; Linux shows "fuse".
  # We grep for the mount path itself for cross-platform consistency.
  if [ -d "$MOUNT_POINT" ] && mount | grep -q "$MOUNT_POINT"; then
    echo "PASS: Mount detected at $MOUNT_POINT"
    exit 0
  fi

  sleep "$INTERVAL"
  ELAPSED=$((ELAPSED + INTERVAL))
done

echo "FAIL: Mount not detected after ${TIMEOUT}s"
exit 1

# wait-for-mount.ps1 -- Poll until the CipherBox FUSE mount point is available.
#
# Usage: .\wait-for-mount.ps1 [-MountPoint <path>]
#   -MountPoint  Path to check (default: $env:USERPROFILE\CipherBox)
#
# Environment:
#   MOUNT_TIMEOUT  Seconds to wait before failing (default: 90)

param(
    [string]$MountPoint = "$env:USERPROFILE\CipherBox"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$Timeout = if ($env:MOUNT_TIMEOUT) { [int]$env:MOUNT_TIMEOUT } else { 90 }
$Interval = 2
$Elapsed = 0

Write-Host "Waiting for mount at $MountPoint (timeout: ${Timeout}s)..."

while ($Elapsed -lt $Timeout) {
    if (Test-Path $MountPoint) {
        Write-Host "PASS: Mount detected at $MountPoint"
        exit 0
    }

    Start-Sleep -Seconds $Interval
    $Elapsed += $Interval
}

Write-Host "FAIL: Mount not detected after ${Timeout}s"
exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# run-all.sh -- Orchestrate the full desktop E2E test suite.
#
# Runs wait-for-mount, FUSE file I/O tests, and API round-trip tests.
# Reports an aggregate pass/fail summary and exits with the total failure count.
#
# Environment:
#   MOUNT_POINT   Path to FUSE mount (default: $HOME/CipherBox)
#   API_URL       Backend API URL (default: http://localhost:3000)
#   TEST_SECRET   test-login shared secret (default: e2e-test-secret-ci-only)

MOUNT_POINT="${MOUNT_POINT:-$HOME/CipherBox}"
API_URL="${API_URL:-http://localhost:3000}"
TEST_SECRET="${TEST_SECRET:-e2e-test-secret-ci-only}"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

TOTAL_PASS=0
TOTAL_FAIL=0

echo "============================================"
echo "  CipherBox Desktop E2E Test Suite"
echo "============================================"
echo ""
echo "Mount point: $MOUNT_POINT"
echo "API URL:     $API_URL"
echo ""

# ---- Step 1: Wait for mount ----
echo "--- Step 1: Wait for mount ---"
if bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/wait-for-mount.sh" "$MOUNT_POINT"; then
  TOTAL_PASS=$((TOTAL_PASS + 1))
else
  echo "FATAL: Mount not available. Cannot continue."
  exit 1
fi
echo ""

# ---- Step 2: FUSE file operations ----
echo "--- Step 2: FUSE file operations ---"
set +e
bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/test-fuse-operations.sh" "$MOUNT_POINT"
FUSE_FAILURES=$?
set -e

if [ "$FUSE_FAILURES" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "FUSE operations: ALL PASSED"
else
  echo "FUSE operations: $FUSE_FAILURES FAILURE(S)"
  TOTAL_FAIL=$((TOTAL_FAIL + FUSE_FAILURES))
fi
echo ""

# ---- Step 3: API round-trip ----
echo "--- Step 3: API round-trip ---"
set +e
bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/test-round-trip.sh" "$MOUNT_POINT" "$API_URL" "$TEST_SECRET"
RT_FAILURES=$?
set -e

if [ "$RT_FAILURES" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "API round-trip: ALL PASSED"
else
  echo "API round-trip: $RT_FAILURES FAILURE(S)"
  TOTAL_FAIL=$((TOTAL_FAIL + RT_FAILURES))
fi
echo ""

# ---- Summary ----
echo "============================================"
echo "  Summary"
echo "============================================"
echo "  Total failures: $TOTAL_FAIL"
echo "============================================"

exit "$TOTAL_FAIL"

retention-days: 1
    name: Build Linux Desktop
    needs: [changes, cargo-check-linux, typecheck]
    if: |
      !failure() && !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'push' || needs.changes.outputs.desktop == 'true')
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            libssl-dev \
            libxdo-dev \
            libfuse3-dev \
            pkg-config \
            build-essential

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: rustup default stable

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            apps/desktop/src-tauri/target
          key: linux-cargo-${{ hashFiles('apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: linux-cargo-

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build crypto package
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build

      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        with:
          projectPath: apps/desktop
          tauriScript: pnpm tauri
          args: -- --no-default-features --features fuse

1→//! AES-256-CTR encryption/decryption.
     2→//!
     3→//! Symmetric encryption for media file content using CTR mode.
     4→//! CTR mode enables random-access decryption (any byte range without
     5→//! processing preceding bytes), required for streaming media playback.
     6→//!
     7→//! Uses Ctr64BE (big-endian 64-bit counter) to match Web Crypto API's
     8→//! `AES-CTR` with `length: 64`.
     9→//!
    10→//! SECURITY NOTE: AES-CTR does NOT provide authentication (unlike GCM).
    11→//! Integrity is provided by IPFS content addressing.
    12→
    13→use aes::Aes256;
    14→use ctr::cipher::{KeyIvInit, StreamCipher};
    15→use thiserror::Error;
    16→
    17→/// AES-CTR IV size in bytes (128-bit counter block).
    18→pub const AES_CTR_IV_SIZE: usize = 16;
    19→
    20→/// AES block size in bytes.
    21→const AES_BLOCK_SIZE: usize = 16;
    22→
    23→/// Type alias for AES-256-CTR with 64-bit big-endian counter.
    24→/// Matches Web Crypto API's `AES-CTR` with `length: 64`.
    25→type Aes256Ctr64BE = ctr::Ctr64BE<Aes256>;
    26→
    27→#[derive(Debug, Error)]
    28→pub enum AesCtrError {
    29→    #[error("Invalid key size")]
    30→    InvalidKeySize,
    31→    #[error("Invalid IV size")]
    32→    InvalidIvSize,
    33→    #[error("Encryption failed")]
    34→    EncryptionFailed,
    35→    #[error("Decryption failed")]
    36→    DecryptionFailed,
    37→    #[error("Invalid range")]
    38→    InvalidRange,
    39→}
    40→
    41→/// Encrypt data using AES-256-CTR.
    42→///
    43→/// Each encryption MUST use a unique IV (nonce + counter) with the same key.
    44→/// Reusing nonce+key pairs is catastrophic for AES-CTR security.
    45→///
    46→/// CTR output is the same size as the input (no authentication tag).
    47→pub fn encrypt_aes_ctr(
    48→    plaintext: &[u8],
    49→    key: &[u8; 32],
    50→    iv: &[u8; 16],
    51→) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AesCtrError> {

    54→

    56→    cipher.apply_keystream(&mut output);

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# test-fuse-operations.sh -- Exercise FUSE mount file I/O operations.
#
# Usage: ./test-fuse-operations.sh [mount-point]
#   mount-point  Path to FUSE mount (default: $HOME/CipherBox)
#
# Tests: create, read, overwrite, mkdir, nested write, binary round-trip,
#        rename, delete file, delete directory.
#
# Exit code: number of failed tests (0 = all passed).

MP="${1:-$HOME/CipherBox}"
PASS=0
FAIL=0

# Detect SHA-256 command (macOS vs Linux)
if command -v shasum &>/dev/null; then
  SHA256_CMD="shasum -a 256"
elif command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null; then
  SHA256_CMD="sha256sum"
else
  echo "FAIL: No SHA-256 command found (shasum or sha256sum)"
  exit 1
fi

pass() {
  PASS=$((PASS + 1))
  echo "PASS: $1"
}

fail() {
  FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
  echo "FAIL: $1"
}

echo "=== FUSE File I/O Tests ==="
echo "Mount point: $MP"
echo ""

# ---- Test 1: Create and read text file ----
echo "--- Test 1: Create and read text file ---"
echo "Hello from CI" > "$MP/e2e-test.txt"
sleep 3
CONTENT=$(cat "$MP/e2e-test.txt")
if [ "$CONTENT" = "Hello from CI" ]; then
  pass "Create and read text file"
else
  fail "Create and read text file (got: '$CONTENT')"
fi

# ---- Test 2: Create directory ----
echo "--- Test 2: Create directory ---"
mkdir -p "$MP/e2e-folder"
if [ -d "$MP/e2e-folder" ]; then
  pass "Create directory"
else
  fail "Create directory"
fi

# ---- Test 3: Write file in subdirectory ----
echo "--- Test 3: Write file in subdirectory ---"
echo "Nested content" > "$MP/e2e-folder/nested.txt"
sleep 3
NESTED=$(cat "$MP/e2e-folder/nested.txt")
if [ "$NESTED" = "Nested content" ]; then
  pass "Write file in subdirectory"
else
  fail "Write file in subdirectory (got: '$NESTED')"
fi

# ---- Test 4: Overwrite file (modify) ----
echo "--- Test 4: Overwrite file ---"
echo "Modified content" > "$MP/e2e-test.txt"
sleep 3
MODIFIED=$(cat "$MP/e2e-test.txt")
if [ "$MODIFIED" = "Modified content" ]; then
  pass "Overwrite file"
else
  fail "Overwrite file (got: '$MODIFIED')"
fi

# ---- Test 5: Binary file round-trip ----
echo "--- Test 5: Binary file round-trip ---"
dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/e2e-binary.bin bs=1024 count=256 2>/dev/null
cp /tmp/e2e-binary.bin "$MP/e2e-binary.bin"
sleep 5
CHECKSUM_ORIG=$($SHA256_CMD /tmp/e2e-binary.bin | cut -d' ' -f1)
CHECKSUM_MOUNT=$($SHA256_CMD "$MP/e2e-binary.bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)
if [ "$CHECKSUM_ORIG" = "$CHECKSUM_MOUNT" ]; then
  pass "Binary file round-trip (256KB)"
else
  fail "Binary file round-trip (orig: $CHECKSUM_ORIG, mount: $CHECKSUM_MOUNT)"
fi

# ---- Test 6: Rename file ----
echo "--- Test 6: Rename file ---"
mv "$MP/e2e-test.txt" "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt"
sleep 2
if [ ! -f "$MP/e2e-test.txt" ] && [ -f "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt" ]; then
  RENAMED=$(cat "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt")
  if [ "$RENAMED" = "Modified content" ]; then
    pass "Rename file"
  else
    fail "Rename file (content changed: '$RENAMED')"
  fi
else
  fail "Rename file (old exists: $(test -f "$MP/e2e-test.txt" && echo yes || echo no), new exists: $(test -f "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt" && echo yes || echo no))"
fi

# ---- Test 7: Delete file ----
echo "--- Test 7: Delete file ---"
rm "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt"
sleep 2
if [ ! -f "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt" ]; then
  pass "Delete file"
else
  fail "Delete file (still exists)"
fi

# ---- Test 8: Delete directory ----
echo "--- Test 8: Delete directory ---"
rm -rf "$MP/e2e-folder"
sleep 2
if [ ! -d "$MP/e2e-folder" ]; then
  pass "Delete directory"
else
  fail "Delete directory (still exists)"
fi

# ---- Test 9: Cleanup ----
echo "--- Test 9: Cleanup ---"
rm -f "$MP/e2e-binary.bin" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f /tmp/e2e-binary.bin 2>/dev/null || true
# Filter .DS_Store from any remaining file checks
REMAINING=$(ls "$MP" 2>/dev/null | grep -v '\.DS_Store' | grep -v '^$' || true)
if [ -z "$REMAINING" ]; then
  pass "Cleanup (mount point clean)"
else
  # Not a hard failure -- other files may be present from the desktop app
  pass "Cleanup (remaining files: $REMAINING)"
fi

# ---- Summary ----
echo ""
echo "=== FUSE File I/O Results ==="
echo "  Passed: $PASS"
echo "  Failed: $FAIL"
echo "=============================="

exit "$FAIL"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# test-round-trip.sh -- Verify desktop FUSE writes are visible via the API.
#
# Usage: ./test-round-trip.sh [mount-point] [api-url] [test-secret]
#   mount-point  Path to FUSE mount (default: $HOME/CipherBox)
#   api-url      Backend API URL (default: http://localhost:3000)
#   test-secret  Shared secret for test-login (default: e2e-test-secret-ci-only)
#
# The server is zero-knowledge -- it cannot decrypt file contents.
# These tests prove the pipeline: FUSE write -> encrypt -> IPFS upload -> IPNS publish -> API visibility.
#
# Exit code: number of failed tests (0 = all passed).

MP="${1:-$HOME/CipherBox}"
API_URL="${2:-http://localhost:3000}"
SECRET="${3:-e2e-test-secret-ci-only}"
TEST_EMAIL="e2e-desktop-rt-$(date +%s)@test.local"

PASS=0
FAIL=0

pass() {
  PASS=$((PASS + 1))
  echo "PASS: $1"
}

fail() {
  FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
  echo "FAIL: $1"
}

echo "=== API Round-Trip Tests ==="
echo "Mount point: $MP"
echo "API URL:     $API_URL"
echo "Test email:  $TEST_EMAIL"
echo ""

# ---- Test 1: Authenticate via test-login ----
echo "--- Test 1: Authenticate via test-login ---"
AUTH_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "$API_URL/auth/test-login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"email\":\"$TEST_EMAIL\",\"secret\":\"$SECRET\"}")

ACCESS_TOKEN=$(echo "$AUTH_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.accessToken // empty')
if [ -n "$ACCESS_TOKEN" ]; then
  pass "Authenticate via test-login"
else
  fail "Authenticate via test-login (response: $AUTH_RESPONSE)"
  echo "FATAL: Cannot proceed without authentication."
  echo ""
  echo "=== API Round-Trip Results ==="
  echo "  Passed: $PASS"
  echo "  Failed: $FAIL"
  echo "==============================="
  exit "$FAIL"
fi

# ---- Test 2: Desktop writes file, API verifies vault exists ----
echo "--- Test 2: Verify vault has content after FUSE write ---"
echo "API-visible content" > "$MP/rt-test.txt"
sleep 5

VAULT_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  "$API_URL/vault")

ROOT_IPNS=$(echo "$VAULT_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.rootIpnsName // empty')
if [ -n "$ROOT_IPNS" ] && [ "$ROOT_IPNS" != "null" ]; then
  pass "Vault has rootIpnsName after FUSE write ($ROOT_IPNS)"
else
  fail "Vault has no rootIpnsName (response: $VAULT_RESPONSE)"
fi

# ---- Test 3: Verify IPNS resolve returns data ----
echo "--- Test 3: Verify IPNS resolve returns CID ---"
if [ -n "$ROOT_IPNS" ] && [ "$ROOT_IPNS" != "null" ]; then
  IPNS_RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
    "$API_URL/ipns/$ROOT_IPNS/resolve")

  # The resolve response should contain a CID (starts with "bafy" or "Qm" or similar)
  RESOLVED_CID=$(echo "$IPNS_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.cid // .value // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "$RESOLVED_CID" ] && [ "$RESOLVED_CID" != "null" ]; then
    pass "IPNS resolve returned CID ($RESOLVED_CID)"
  else

1→# Summary Template
     2→
     3→Template for `.planning/phases/XX-name/{phase}-{plan}-SUMMARY.md` - phase completion documentation.
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## File Template
     8→
     9→```markdown
    10→---
    11→phase: XX-name
    12→plan: YY
    13→subsystem: [primary category: auth, payments, ui, api, database, infra, testing, etc.]
    14→tags: [searchable tech: jwt, stripe, react, postgres, prisma]
    15→
    16→# Dependency graph
    17→requires:
    18→  - phase: [prior phase this depends on]
    19→    provides: [what that phase built that this uses]
    20→provides:
    21→  - [bullet list of what this phase built/delivered]
    22→affects: [list of phase names or keywords that will need this context]
    23→
    24→# Tech tracking
    25→tech-stack:
    26→  added: [libraries/tools added in this phase]
    27→  patterns: [architectural/code patterns established]
    28→
    29→key-files:
    30→  created: [important files created]
    31→  modified: [important files modified]
    32→
    33→key-decisions:
    34→  - "Decision 1"
    35→  - "Decision 2"
    36→
    37→patterns-established:
    38→  - "Pattern 1: description"
    39→  - "Pattern 2: description"
    40→
    41→# Metrics
    42→duration: Xmin
    43→completed: YYYY-MM-DD
    44→---
    45→
    46→# Phase [X]: [Name] Summary
    47→
    48→**[Substantive one-liner describing outcome - NOT "phase complete" or "implementation finished"]**
    49→
    50→## Performance
    51→
    52→- **Duration:** [time] (e.g., 23 min, 1h 15m)
    53→- **Started:** [ISO timestamp]
    54→- **Completed:** [ISO timestamp]
    55→- **Tasks:** [count completed]
    56→- **Files modified:** [count]
    57→
    58→## Accomplishments
    59→- [Most important outcome]
    60→- [Second key accomplishment]
    61→- [Third if applicable]
    62→
    63→## Task Commits
    64→
    65→Each task was committed atomically:
    66→
    67→1. **Task 1: [task name]** - `abc123f` (feat/fix/test/refactor)
    68→2. **Task 2: [task name]** - `def456g` (feat/fix/test/refactor)
    69→3. **Task 3: [task name]** - `hij789k` (feat/fix/test/refactor)
    70→
    71→**Plan metadata:** `lmn012o` (docs: complete plan)
    72→
    73→_Note: TDD tasks may have multiple commits (test → feat → refactor)_
    74→
    75→## Files Created/Modified
    76→- `path/to/file.ts` - What it does
    77→- `path/to/another.ts` - What it does
    78→
    79→## Decisions Made
    80→[Key decisions with brief rationale, or "None - followed plan as specified"]
    81→
    82→## Deviations from Plan
    83→
    84→[If no deviations: "None - plan executed exactly as written"]
    85→
    86→[If deviations occurred:]
    87→
    88→### Auto-fixed Issues
    89→
    90→**1. [Rule X - Category] Brief description**
    91→- **Found during:** Task [N] ([task name])
    92→- **Issue:** [What was wrong]
    93→- **Fix:** [What was done]
    94→- **Files modified:** [file paths]
    95→- **Verification:** [How it was verified]
    96→- **Committed in:** [hash] (part of task commit)
    97→
    98→[... repeat for each auto-fix ...]
    99→
   100→---
   101→
   102→**Total deviations:** [N] auto-fixed ([breakdown by rule])
   103→**Impact on plan:** [Brief assessment - e.g., "All auto-fixes necessary for correctness/security. No scope creep."]
   104→
   105→## Issues Encountered
   106→[Problems and how they were resolved, or "None"]
   107→
   108→[Note: "Deviations from Plan" documents unplanned work that was handled automatically via deviation rules. "Issues Encountered" documents problems during planned work that required problem-solving.]
   109→
   110→## User Setup Required
   111→
   112→[If USER-SETUP.md was generated:]
   113→**External services require manual configuration.** See [{phase}-USER-SETUP.md](./{phase}-USER-SETUP.md) for:
   114→- Environment variables to add
   115→- Dashboard configuration steps
   116→- Verification commands
   117→
   118→[If no USER-SETUP.md:]
   119→None - no external service configuration required.
   120→
   121→## Next Phase Readiness
   122→[What's ready for next phase]
   123→[Any blockers or concerns]
   124→
   125→---
   126→*Phase: XX-name*
   127→*Completed: [date]*
   128→```
   129→
   130→<frontmatter_guidance>
   131→**Purpose:** Enable automatic context assembly via dependency graph. Frontmatter makes summary metadata machine-readable so plan-phase can scan all summaries quickly and select relevant ones based on dependencies.
   132→
   133→**Fast scanning:** Frontmatter is first ~25 lines, cheap to scan across all summaries without reading full content.
   134→
   135→**Dependency graph:** `requires`/`provides`/`affects` create explicit links between phases, enabling transitive closure for context selection.
   136→
   137→**Subsystem:** Primary categorization (auth, payments, ui, api, database, infra, testing) for detecting related phases.
   138→
   139→**Tags:** Searchable technical keywords (libraries, frameworks, tools) for tech stack awareness.
   140→
   141→**Key-files:** Important files for @context references in PLAN.md.
   142→
   143→**Patterns:** Established conventions future phases should maintain.
   144→
   145→**Population:** Frontmatter is populated during summary creation in execute-plan.md. See `<step name="create_summary">` for field-by-field guidance.
   146→</frontmatter_guidance>
   147→
   148→<one_liner_rules>
   149→The one-liner MUST be substantive:
   150→
   151→**Good:**
   152→- "JWT auth with refresh rotation using jose library"
   153→- "Prisma schema with User, Session, and Product models"
   154→- "Dashboard with real-time metrics via Server-Sent Events"
   155→
   156→**Bad:**
   157→- "Phase complete"
   158→- "Authentication implemented"
   159→- "Foundation finished"
   160→- "All tasks done"
   161→
   162→The one-liner should tell someone what actually shipped.
   163→</one_liner_rules>
   164→
   165→<example>
   166→```markdown
   167→# Phase 1: Foundation Summary
   168→
   169→**JWT auth with refresh rotation using jose library, Prisma User model, and protected API middleware**
   170→
   171→## Performance
   172→
   173→- **Duration:** 28 min
   174→- **Started:** 2025-01-15T14:22:10Z
   175→- **Completed:** 2025-01-15T14:50:33Z
   176→- **Tasks:** 5
   177→- **Files modified:** 8
   178→
   179→## Accomplishments
   180→- User model with email/password auth
   181→- Login/logout endpoints with httpOnly JWT cookies
   182→- Protected route middleware checking token validity
   183→- Refresh token rotation on each request
   184→
   185→## Files Created/Modified
   186→- `prisma/schema.prisma` - User and Session models
   187→- `src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts` - Login endpoint
   188→- `src/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts` - Logout endpoint
   189→- `src/middleware.ts` - Protected route checks
   190→- `src/lib/auth.ts` - JWT helpers using jose
   191→
   192→## Decisions Made
   193→- Used jose instead of jsonwebtoken (ESM-native, Edge-compatible)
   194→- 15-min access tokens with 7-day refresh tokens
   195→- Storing refresh tokens in database for revocation capability
   196→
   197→## Deviations from Plan
   198→
   199→### Auto-fixed Issues
   200→
   201→**1. [Rule 2 - Missing Critical] Added password hashing with bcrypt**
   202→- **Found during:** Task 2 (Login endpoint implementation)

# Phase 11.4 Plan 02: Test Scripts Summary

**8 cross-platform test scripts (bash + PowerShell) covering 9 FUSE file I/O operations and 3 API round-trip verifications with parameterized mount points**

## Performance

- **Duration:** 10 min
- **Started:** 2026-02-28T19:07:54Z
- **Completed:** 2026-02-28T19:18:30Z
- **Tasks:** 2/2
- **Files created:** 8

## Accomplishments

- Created wait-for-mount scripts that poll mount point availability with configurable 90s timeout
- Created run-all orchestrator scripts that chain mount wait, FUSE tests, and API round-trip with aggregate reporting
- Created FUSE file I/O test scripts with 9 test cases: create, read, overwrite, mkdir, nested write, binary round-trip (256KB with SHA-256 verification), rename, delete file, delete directory
- Created API round-trip test scripts with 3 test cases: test-login auth, vault verification, IPNS resolve

## Task Commits

Each task was committed atomically:

1. **Task 1: Create wait-for-mount and run-all orchestrator scripts** - `51aec33d5` (feat)
2. **Task 2: Create FUSE file I/O and API round-trip test scripts** - `f44d4d697` (feat)

## Files Created

- `tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/wait-for-mount.sh` - Poll mount point with timeout (macOS/Linux)
- `tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/wait-for-mount.ps1` - Poll mount point with timeout (Windows)
- `tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/run-all.sh` - Orchestrate full test suite (macOS/Linux)
- `tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/run-all.ps1` - Orchestrate full test suite (Windows)
- `tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/test-fuse-operations.sh` - 9 FUSE file I/O test cases (macOS/Linux)
- `tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/test-fuse-operations.ps1` - 9 FUSE file I/O test cases (Windows)
- `tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/test-round-trip.sh` - 3 API round-trip test cases (macOS/Linux)
- `tests/e2e-desktop/scripts/test-round-trip.ps1` - 3 API round-trip test cases (Windows)

## Decisions Made

- **Invoke-RestMethod over Invoke-WebRequest:** PowerShell round-trip scripts use `Invoke-RestMethod` which auto-parses JSON responses, eliminating the need for manual `ConvertFrom-Json` calls. The plan's task description explicitly specified this cmdlet.
- **Exit code = failure count:** Test scripts exit with the number of failed tests rather than simple 0/1, allowing the orchestrator to aggregate total failures across all test suites.
- **Cross-platform SHA-256 detection:** FUSE operations script auto-detects `shasum -a 256` (macOS) vs `sha256sum` (Linux) at startup to handle binary file verification.

## Deviations from Plan

None - plan executed exactly as written.

## Issues Encountered

- **1Password signing agent failures:** The 1Password SSH agent consistently returned "failed to fill whole buffer" errors during commit signing. Commits were created unsigned (acceptable per project policy -- PRs are squash-merged by GitHub with its own signature). One commit (Task 2, `f44d4d697`) was merged with Plan 01 fixture files by a parallel agent's lint-staged interaction, resulting in a mismatched commit message.

## User Setup Required

None - no external service configuration required.

## Next Phase Readiness

- All 8 test scripts ready for consumption by `e2e-desktop.yml` workflow (Plan 03)
- run-all.sh/ps1 is the single entry point the workflow will invoke
- Scripts accept `MOUNT_POINT`, `API_URL`, and `TEST_SECRET` environment variables for CI configuration

    61→Decisions are logged in PROJECT.md Key Decisions table.
    62→Recent decisions affecting current work:
    63→
    64→| Decision                                                               | Phase     | Rationale                                                                                                            |
    65→| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    66→| Replace PnP Modal SDK with MPC Core Kit                                | Phase 12  | Full MFA control, custom UX, programmatic factor mgmt                                                                |
    67→| CipherBox as identity provider (sub=userId)                            | Phase 12  | Enables multi-auth linking, less data to Web3Auth                                                                    |
    68→| Identity trilemma: chose (wallet-only + unified) w/ SPOF               | Phase 12  | No mandatory email; SPOF mitigated by key export+IPFS                                                                |
    69→| Phase 12 split into 12, 12.2, 12.3, 12.4                               | Phase 12  | Foundation->device registry->SIWE->MFA dependency chain                                                              |
    70→| Core Kit WEB3AUTH_NETWORK uses DEVNET/MAINNET keys                     | 12-02     | Different from PnP SDK's SAPPHIRE_DEVNET/SAPPHIRE_MAINNET                                                            |
    71→| CipherBox JWT for backend auth (not coreKit.signatures)                | 12-04     | Core Kit signatures are session tokens, not verifiable JWTs. Pass CipherBox-issued JWT with loginType 'corekit'      |
    72→| importTssKey via localStorage one-time read-and-delete                 | 12-05     | PnP migration key consumed once then removed                                                                         |
    73→| E2E uses CipherBox login UI directly (no modal iframe)                 | 12-05     | Simpler, more reliable than Web3Auth modal automation                                                                |
    74→| jose library for identity JWTs (not @nestjs/jwt)                       | 12-01     | Separate signing keys (RS256) and audience from internal                                                             |
    75→| Cross-auth-method email linking                                        | 12-01     | Same email across Google/email auth -> same user account                                                             |
    76→| ECIES re-wrapping for sharing (not proxy re-encryption)                | Research  | Same wrapKey() function, server sees only ciphertexts                                                                |
    77→| Versioning = stop unpinning old CIDs + metadata extension              | Research  | Nearly free on IPFS, no new crypto needed                                                                            |
    78→| Read-only sharing only (no multi-writer IPNS)                          | Research  | Unsolved problem, deferred to v3                                                                                     |
    79→| minisearch + idb for client-side search                                | Research  | ~8KB total, TypeScript-native, zero server interaction                                                               |
    80→| Wallet addr: SHA-256 hash + truncated display (no encrypt)             | 12.3-01   | Simpler than hash+encrypted; full plaintext never stored                                                             |
    81→| Auth types: email_passwordless->email, external_wallet->wallet         | 12.3-01   | Clean method-based naming for simplified auth type system                                                            |
    82→| derivationVersion removed (ADR-001 clean break)                        | 12.3-01   | DB will be wiped, no migration needed, clean Core Kit-only schema                                                    |
    83→| Web3AuthVerifierService decoupled from auth.service                    | 12.3-02   | No longer injected; all login/link flows use CipherBox JWT verification                                              |
    84→| LinkMethodDto uses auth method types directly                          | 12.3-02   | google/email/wallet instead of routing through social/external_wallet loginType                                      |
    85→| Vault export derivationInfo simplified to derivationMethod             | 12.3-02   | Always 'web3auth' for Core Kit users; no derivationVersion needed                                                    |
    86→| connectAsync for wallet SIWE flow (not useEffect-based)                | 12.3-03   | Simpler async flow; avoids address-watching complexity                                                               |
    87→| Disconnect wagmi after SIWE verification                               | 12.3-03   | No persistent wallet connection needed; Core Kit handles ongoing auth                                                |
    88→| vaultKeypair naming for auth store keypair                             | 12.3-03   | Clear purpose naming; replaces misleading ADR-001 derivedKeypair                                                     |
    89→| Reuse login components in link mode (settings)                         | 12.3-04   | GoogleLoginButton/EmailLoginForm reused via callback props; no separate link components                              |
    90→| Multiple wallets allowed per account                                   | 12.3-04   | Wallet always shows as available to link; CONTEXT.md requirement                                                     |
    91→| Cross-account collision via TypeORM Not()                              | 12.3-04   | Check same identifier with different userId before allowing link                                                     |
    92→| Vault IPNS: same salt, different HKDF info for domain separation       | 12.3.1-01 | HKDF info is primary domain separator; "cipherbox-vault-ipns-v1" vs registry's info                                  |
    93→| rootIpnsPublicKey removed from EncryptedVaultKeys                      | 12.3.1-01 | Derivable from private key; reduces stored data, eliminates inconsistency                                            |
    94→| Google login hashes sub (not email) for identifierHash                 | 12.3.1-02 | Sub is immutable Google user ID; email can change. Privacy-preserving lookup.                                        |
    95→| Cross-method email auto-linking removed                                | 12.3.1-02 | Each auth method is independent; users link explicitly via Settings, not auto-linked by email match                  |
    96→| identifier column stores hash for all auth types                       | 12.3.1-02 | identifier=identifierHash for consistency; identifierDisplay holds human-readable value                              |
    97→| rootIpnsPublicKey removed from vault entity/DTO/API/frontend           | 12.3.1-03 | Derivable from privateKey via HKDF; reduces schema, eliminates inconsistency                                         |
    98→| Plan 04 work completed by Plan 03 broader scope                        | 12.3.1-04 | Desktop Rust, E2E helpers, controller spec changes committed in Plan 03 execution                                    |
    99→| Auto-expire on read (no cron for 5min TTL)                             | 12.4-01   | Pending requests past TTL marked expired on getStatus; simpler than background cleanup                               |
   100→| Hard delete on cancel (not status change)                              | 12.4-01   | Cancelled requests have no audit value; 5min TTL keeps table small                                                   |
   101→| loginWithCoreKit returns typed union (not void)                        | 12.4-02   | 'logged_in' or 'required_share' enables callers to branch without catching errors                                    |
   102→| Placeholder publicKey for REQUIRED_SHARE temp auth                     | 12.4-02   | 'pending-core-kit-{userId}' allows bulletin board API access before TSS key available                                |
   103→| Pending auth state in React useState (not Zustand)                     | 12.4-02   | Component-scoped, cleared on unmount or logout; no need for global persistence                                       |
   104→| FactorInfo extended with additionalMetadata for device matching        | 12.4-03   | Core Kit shareDescriptions parsed to expose deviceId for factor-to-device matching                                   |
   105→| ARIA tablist/tabpanel for Settings tab navigation                      | 12.4-03   | Proper accessibility roles for tab switching between Linked Methods and Security                                     |
   106→| Inline confirm pattern for destructive MFA actions                     | 12.4-03   | Revoke/regenerate use inline confirm/cancel, not modal dialog, matching terminal aesthetic                           |

   109→| DeviceApprovalModal mounted in AppShell after AppFooter                | 12.4-04   | Fixed overlay visible on all authenticated pages regardless of current route                                         |
   110→| LoginFooter extracted to avoid duplication in Login.tsx                | 12.4-04   | Three render paths (normal, waiting, recovery) share the same footer component                                       |
   111→| Generated client wrapper pattern for device-approval service           | 12.4-05   | deviceApprovalApi wraps Orval-generated functions for backward-compatible import surface                             |
   112→| tssPubKey defensive check as permanent enableMfa() guard               | 12.4-05   | Logs CRITICAL if keypair changes after MFA enrollment; does not throw (enrollment already succeeded)                 |

   114→| Merge Settings.tsx into SettingsPage (not re-route)                    | 12.5-01   | SettingsPage is canonical routed component with AppShell; merging preserves existing routing and layout              |
   115→| Hardhat account #0 for wallet E2E test key                             | 12.5-02   | Well-known deterministic key; reproducible tests without real wallet funds                                           |
   116→| Wallet E2E tests validate UI flow independently of Core Kit            | 12.5-02   | TC09 accepts both redirect-to-files and error as valid; tests frontend wallet interaction                            |
   117→| UAT quality gate: 16 PASS / 19 SKIP / 1 NOTE (all documented)          | 12.5-03   | Destructive and multi-device tests skipped with reasons; all 4 issues resolved; gate passed for Phase 12.1           |

   120→| fileId minimum 10 chars validation                                     | 12.6-01   | Ensures UUID-length identifiers; prevents accidental short strings in HKDF info                                      |
   121→| Partial success for batch publish (per-record results)                 | 12.6-02   | Failed records logged and counted, not re-thrown; batch returns totalSucceeded/totalFailed                           |

   183→| readOnly prop on ContextMenu for shared context                        | 14-05     | Same component serves owned and shared contexts; clean conditional without separate component                        |
   184→| NavItem icon map with Unicode characters                               | 14-05     | Consistent with terminal aesthetic; no SVG icons needed for sidebar navigation                                       |
   185→| Dynamic import() for checkAndRotateIfNeeded circular dep               | 14-06     | share.service imports folder.store; folder.service importing share.service creates circular; dynamic import() defers |
   186→| Lazy rotation defers parent metadata update to caller                  | 14-06     | checkAndRotateIfNeeded returns new key + rotated flag; caller handles parent folderKeyEncrypted update               |
   187→| Post-upload re-wrapping is fire-and-forget                             | 14-06     | Non-blocking: failures logged but never delay upload completion UI                                                   |
   188→| FileAttrs with to_fuse_attr() boundary conversion                      | 11-01     | Core uses platform-agnostic FileAttrs; uid/gid injected at operations layer, not stored in shared structs            |
   189→| AccessMode enum replaces libc POSIX flags                              | 11-01     | Platform-independent ReadOnly/WriteOnly/ReadWrite instead of O_RDONLY/O_WRONLY/O_RDWR                                |
   190→| cfg(any(fuse, winfsp)) for shared filesystem code                      | 11-01     | Shared types available to both platforms; mount/unmount remain feature-specific                                      |
   191→| Self-contained decrypt functions per platform module                   | 11-02     | Windows module has own decrypt_metadata_from_ipfs; fuse::operations gated to fuse-only, can't be cross-referenced    |
   192→| Arc<Mutex<CipherBoxFS>> for WinFsp interior mutability                 | 11-02     | WinFsp callbacks receive &self; Mutex wraps shared state for safe mutation from any thread                           |
   193→| OnceLock<AtomicBool> stop signal for WinFsp unmount                    | 11-02     | Avoids storing FileSystemHost globally; stop flag coordinates shutdown across threads                                |
   194→| WinFsp creates mount directory (no pre-create)                         | 11-02     | WinFsp uses reparse point for mount; pre-existing directory causes mount failure                                     |
   195→| Platform dispatch via cfg re-exports in fuse/mod.rs                    | 11-02     | Same function names (mount_filesystem/unmount_filesystem) resolve to correct impl via feature flags                  |
   196→| WinFsp runtime detection via winreg at startup                         | 11-03     | Registry check + DLL existence verification; notification if missing, app still launches                             |
   197→| NSIS ExecWait for WinFsp MSI install (not nsExec)                      | 11-03     | Simpler exit code handling; MSI installed silently with INSTALLLEVEL=1000                                            |
   198→| WinFsp MSI downloaded in CI, not committed to git                      | 11-03     | Binary files not suitable for source control; CI downloads from official GitHub release                              |
   199→| cfg(any(fuse, winfsp)) in entry point files                            | 11-03     | Compound feature gate enables same mount/unmount code paths on both platforms                                        |

   204→| secp256k1.keygen() for ephemeral invite keypairs                       | 15-02     | Noble v3 API uses keygen() returning { secretKey, publicKey }; matches useDeviceApproval pattern                     |

1→# Phase 11.4: Cross-Platform E2E Testing - Context
     2→
     3→**Gathered:** 2026-02-28
     4→**Status:** Ready for planning
     5→
     6→<domain>
     7→## Phase Boundary
     8→
     9→Validate that each desktop client (Windows, macOS, Linux) can round-trip correctly against the API and web client — proving cross-platform data integrity, encryption compatibility, and sync correctness. No new features; this is a testing and CI infrastructure phase only.
    10→
    11→</domain>
    12→
    13→<decisions>
    14→## Implementation Decisions
    15→
    16→### CI backend stack
    17→
    18→- Native Postgres + IPFS installs per platform runner (brew on macOS, chocolatey/scoop on Windows, apt on Linux)
    19→- Fresh NestJS API backend per CI run with empty database — full isolation, no staging pollution
    20→- Cache the cargo-built desktop binary from existing build jobs and download it in the E2E job (avoid rebuilding Rust from scratch)
    21→
    22→### CI trigger strategy
    23→
    24→- Smart trigger: run on PRs only when desktop or crypto paths change (path filter)
    25→- Full cross-platform matrix on pushes to main and release branches
    26→- Manual workflow_dispatch available for ad-hoc runs
    27→
    28→### Test execution model
    29→
    30→- FUSE mount file operations: real file I/O (create, read, write, rename, delete) via standard OS calls through the mounted filesystem
    31→- Install platform FUSE drivers on all three CI runners (FUSE-T on macOS, WinFsp on Windows, libfuse3 on Linux)
    32→- Launch the actual Tauri app binary in test mode (--test flag or env var), not standalone Rust test binary
    33→- Authenticate via dev-key auth (POST /auth/test-login) — no Web3Auth/Core Kit in CI
    34→
    35→### Cross-platform interop
    36→
    37→- Full data round-trip via API: web client uploads, desktop downloads and decrypts (and vice versa)
    38→- Static test vectors (known plaintext/key/ciphertext) as baseline PLUS live API round-trips for integration confidence
    39→- Cover both AES-GCM (standard files) and AES-CTR (media streaming) encryption modes
    40→- Skip ECIES key wrapping interop — already proven in production via desktop device approval
    41→
    42→### Test organization
    43→
    44→- Shared test fixtures checked into git (encrypted test files + keys + expected metadata) as single source of truth for format compatibility
    45→- Desktop-side tests only — don't extend web Playwright for interop (shared test vectors cover web-side validation)
    46→
    47→### Claude's Discretion
    48→
    49→- Where tests live in the monorepo (top-level tests/e2e-desktop/ vs apps/desktop/tests/)
    50→- Test failure reporting format (standard cargo output vs JUnit XML artifacts)
    51→- Virtual framebuffer (Xvfb) setup for headless Tauri on Linux CI
    52→- Specific path filters for the smart trigger
    53→- Test data cleanup strategy between runs
    54→
    55→</decisions>

    58→## Specific Ideas
    59→
    60→- Reuse cached cargo binary artifact from existing CI build jobs rather than rebuilding — saves the full Rust compile step in the E2E job
    61→- Tauri app in test mode gives closest-to-real user experience while still being automatable
    62→
    63→</specifics>

    66→## Deferred Ideas
    67→
    68→None — discussion stayed within phase scope.
